Daily Report — 2026-07-04 Daily Overview What was done: Corrected layout rendering issues for usage metrics, traced cost normalization workflows, and evaluated distributed archive formats for potential deduplication vulnerabilities. How it was done: Overrode conflicting CMS theme CSS selectors to restore grid layouts, performed static analysis on export and merge routines in Python and Rust codebases, and validated data integrity by comparing external JSONL backups against local snapshots. Impact: Restored accurate daily report visualization, established a clear understanding of the cost injection pipeline, and identified critical edge cases in SSH-based device aliasing while preserving historical token costs from source-side rolling deletions. Fixed CSS priority bugs in the token usage summary card, mapped cost data flow and daily report generation pipelines, and conducted a deep architectural analysis of cross-device data synchronization to resolve historical data recovery concerns and alias collision risks.
Tasks Architecture & Strategy ✅ Audit cross-device JSONL export schema and deduplication risks — Decoded source_key vs device semantics, validated OneDrive TokenMonitor backups for historical gaps, and identified alias collision hazards in peer imports. Implementation & Fixes ✅ Fix token usage card layout overflow — Resolved display obstruction by increasing CSS selector specificity for .usage-card__stats, resetting definition list widths, and verifying against formatter tests. ✅ Trace cost pricing injection and report generation pipeline — Mapped totalCost flow through usage.py, confirmed embedding in usage_card.py, and executed local preview workflows using merge/deploy commands. Problems & Solutions Critical Issues 1. Ambiguity in cross-device JSONL export files where identical SSH aliases from different machines would falsely merge distinct hosts upon import, skewing costs. Solution: Defined strict remapping rules via remap_peer_source, confirmed the architecture rewrites peer local:* keys on ingestion, and identified that preserving user-chosen aliases for remote hosts remains a vulnerability requiring stable host fingerprinting to resolve.
Key Insight: Distributed synchronization protocols cannot rely on mutable user configurations as unique identifiers; machine identity must be decoupled from display labels and derived from invariant hardware or network fingerprints to prevent silent data fusion attacks.
2. Risk of permanent historical token cost loss because the source generator’s rolling window deletes past session JSONL files before full archive capture. Solution: Confirmed that save_usage_file employs an idempotent merge strategy on top of existing snapshots, preserving data beyond the source export window; additionally mapped external backup files to reconstruct missing periods.
Key Insight: Aggregation pipelines must implement local history merging as a defensive layer against volatile source exporters; without this, rolling cleanups will create insurmountable gaps in long-term analytics.
General Issues 3. Token usage card collapsed into unreadable vertical text due to PaperMod theme overriding grid styles and forcing fixed column widths on dl/dt/dd elements. Solution: Scoped the CSS reset to .usage-card descendants, increased cascade priority, and explicitly applied width: auto to definition terms and data lists; verified with self-check scripts.
Key Insight: Third-party CMS themes apply broad structural styles (like definition lists) that can silently destroy custom component layouts, requiring strictly targeted selectors rather than relying on standard HTML tag behavior.
Human vs AI Approaches Strategic Level Distribution model vs central merge file for cross-device archives Role Approach Human Advocated for a unified ‘objective’ merged file written by all devices to single-source truth, citing size discrepancies and data convergence concerns. AI Explained the danger of multi-writer race conditions over cloud-synced folders, validated the current per-device write model, and demonstrated how local incremental imports already function as a robust merge engine without central coordination. Difference Analysis: Human focused on logical data unification and schema consistency; AI countered with operational concurrency constraints inherent to file-based synchronization, successfully redirecting the approach away from fragile centralized writes.
AI Limitations General Limitations Initially confused local vs. remote log paths for the daily merge command, requiring user correction to specify exact file paths or sync flags before proceeding with the report workflow. Deferred detailed explanation of JSONL schema fields until directly challenged, missing an opportunity to proactively clarify source_key, device, and record structures during initial export analysis. Learnings Key Learnings Hugo’s markdown rendering with unsafe HTML enables custom components but demands rigorous CSS isolation; standard theme resets and generic tag styles will inevitably collide, making scoped wrappers and high-specificity selectors mandatory for reliable UI embedding. Local-first data sync architectures benefit immensely from single-writer-per-file guarantees combined with peer-side incremental imports; attempting to centralize writes introduces catastrophic concurrency risks that outweigh the benefits of a physical merge file. Key insight: Memory residency and network parser behavior dominate local AI latency; in coordinated workflows, tuning concurrency and KV budgets offers higher ROI than pure token decoding optimization.

Platform security policies blocked automatic cleanup commands, missing API keys caused script pauses, and initial AI proposals ignoring clear user scope boundaries could lead to repository cross-contamination. Solution: Stop operations at the security checkpoint, record environment variables that need manual override, align all configuration changes with user-defined architecture constraints, and prioritize semantic quality checks over aggressive speed tuning.
Key insight: Automated tools require clear environment validation and strict execution boundaries; balancing throughput optimization and verifiable quality boundaries avoids hidden defects and infrastructure waste.

A comprehensive multi-phase refactoring of the Gadget ecosystem was carried out to strengthen infrastructure boundaries, resolve critical automation and visualization errors, reorganize document hierarchy structures, and modernize the translation backend, thereby eliminating silent failures and data loss issues.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Editing-level visualization refactoring and data integrity enhancement — Replaced heavy matplotlib charts with responsive HTML/CSS footer cards matching project design markers, and developed a mtime-based backup tool to prevent deletion of old data during report generation. ✅ Strengthening single-repository architecture and completion of Phase 4 — Completed Phase 1–4 of the refactoring prioritizing security, established a clear backend validation registry, centralized duplicate JSON repair processes, re-encrypted the translation engine cache to prevent cross-backend leaks, and redesigned the cache architecture. ✅ Infrastructure audit and critical error fixes — Conducted deep structural audits, resolved six high-severity defects, including destructive environment cleanup scripts, LLM timeout regressions, E2E configuration isolation gaps, and key translation package encapsulation flaws. ✅ Repository hygiene and contributor identity standardization — Applied .gitignore exclusion rules for sensitive configurations, unified historical commit authors across multiple repositories through forced branch rewrite filtering, and treated the continuous GitHub sidebar avatar as a cached API metadata product. ✅ Translator UI modernization and Ollama OCR backend integration — Designed a strict plain-text Gradio input flow with fixed dimensions, replaced old subprocess-driven approaches with Ollama’s native infinite OCR pipeline, and bypassed damaged chat templates via direct API injection. ✅ Automation pipeline logic correction and formatter strengthening — Replaced simple file existence expiration checks with calendar-based completion tracking and causal mtime detection, while fixing the markdown renderer to safely coerce corrupted LLM-generated cache payloads. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Ollama’s automatic template generation silently breaks custom GGUF chat templates, leading to empty prompts and hallucination outputs, while visual OCR models suffer early EOS termination issues. Solution: Inject verified Jinja templates via direct API calls, add clear stop markers, adjust temperature/retry parameters, and deploy a lightweight parser to remove coordinate metadata from visual responses.
Key Insight: For quantitative architectures, it is impossible to rely on local LLM runners for automatic template generation; hard-coded token processing constraints and strict post-processing are essential conditions for stability.
2. Silent backend fallback chains and fragile JSON unpacking lead to unpredictable scheduling paths, lost payload data, and translator hallucinations. Solution: Implement a clear ALLOWED_BACKENDS constant and throw ValueError early, centralize repair processes with target payload restrictions, and redesign package encapsulation logic to verify pattern integrity before selection.
Key Insight: Trust boundary inputs must be explicitly defined via constants rather than dynamic fallback mechanisms; untrusted model payloads should be validated by pattern priority rather than heuristic matching.
3. Automatic pipelines incorrectly treat weekly/monthly reports as the latest state, and crashes due to binary file checks and strict type assumptions cause cache field corruption. Solution: Replace existence proxies with calendar-based cycle calculators, implement parent mtime decay tracking, and add dynamic type coercion protection for non-dictionary-type overview payloads in the markdown renderer.
Key Insight: The reliability of generative triggers depends on causal time boundaries rather than static file states; formatters for AI outputs must achieve pattern independence.
General Issues 4. Git history rewriting and uncommitted work tree conflicts, along with platform-specific contributor graphs, cause infinite UI synchronization delays. Solution: Execute targeted storage/restore sequences, maintain original state during branch filtering operations, and clarify that GitHub’s lazy cache layer requires standard propagation time or cache rebuild trigger mechanisms.
Key Insight: Version control refactoring requires temporary work tree isolation; platform metadata graphs run independently from the git object tree.
Comparison of Human and AI Approaches Pipeline Logic and Expiration Calculation Role Approach Human Establishes time-centered basic requirements, forces deterministic ISO week/month boundary calculations, and performs direct causal comparisons via proxy timestamps. AI Initially uses file existence proxies, forces single-cycle re calculation, and gradually shifts to calendar-based set checks and mtime decay tracking. Analysis of Differences: Humans provide architectural constraints that eliminate metadata dependencies; AI iterates until precise time boundary calculations and parent-causal verification are achieved.
Visual Architecture and Aesthetic Constraints Role Approach Human Designs strict minimal editing footer cards, requires clear mapping to existing project design markers, enabling seamless integration without manual hex matching. AI Proposes complex interactive dashboards and full data visualization stacks, then correctly redirects to semantic HTML/CSS and strict variable inheritance mechanisms based on user needs. Ollama’s automatic template generation often silently fails or breaks prompt injection when custom or quantitative GGUF architectures are used, without clear diagnostic errors. Daily Report — 2026-06-30 Overall Status Completed Work: Developed a full repository-wide bootstrap mechanism for the Gadget project; resolved hardcoded issues in the summarize CLI worker configuration; fixed SSH proxy and rclone synchronization conflicts; implemented support for the Claude platform on AWS. Implementation Methods: Used a YAML-driven step registry for bootstrapping; refactored the CLI parameter passing mechanism in multiple Python modules to enable dynamic worker quantity adjustment; patched the batch upload feature of remote.py; verified the configuration paths provided by LLM providers. These tasks often got interrupted due to session authentication errors and required manual intervention. Impact: Achieved a flexible, parallel execution mode for the summarize pipeline; simplified the setup process for new devices or environments; corrected critical data transfer failures; however, tool availability issues partially affected productivity. By implementing an elastic bootstrap system, fixing key parallelism and network errors, and configuring AWS-specific LLM routing, the functionality of the Gadget toolkit was significantly improved; but severe operation delays occurred due to continuous authentication failures in Claude Code.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Built a full repository-wide bootstrap system — Created a YAML-driven step registry in scripts/onboard.py to automate SSH, authentication (including the Claude platform on AWS), and plugin installation. Added a step switch function and wrote unit tests. ✅ Implemented a pre-flight bootstrap module for summarize — Created tools/summarize/onboarding.py to check prerequisites (rclone, API keys, Hugo), and integrated the check mechanism into auto.py to prevent execution when requirements are missing. ✅ Resolved SSH proxy port conflict and network setup issues — Found isolated sessions blocking ports 7890/18080; switched to the free port 10087; updated net.sh; configured DNS/proxy bridging for GitHub access in isolated Pods. ✅ Refactored the worker quantity mechanism of the summarize CLI — Replaced the hardcoded os.cpu_count() with args.workers in daily.py; updated __main__.py to accept that parameter, and ensured auto.py can correctly forward that parameter. ✅ Implemented resilient rclone batch upload — Refactored _rclone_upload in remote.py using directory batch transfer and retries; patched scripts/sync.py to gracefully skip missing remote directories during initialization. ✅ Configured routing for Claude platform providers on AWS — Clarified the differences between Bedrock and the Claude platform on AWS, set the correct environment variables CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS, and updated documentation. 🔄 Investigated batch merge failures in summarize — Diagnosed system-level LLM block timeouts among 43 daily merge sub-processes; explored using local HuggingFace models as a strategy to reduce latency. ❌ Login to Claude Code is blocked — Multiple attempts at authentication and starting Claude Code failed; no development work could be done during these sessions. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Fixed outdated editable installation and deployment sites — Regenerated the editable installation finder for summarize CLI, cloned the GitHub Pages repository into public/, and updated the LLM model configuration (Sonnet 5/Opus 4.8). ✅ Integrated documentation into a bilingual format — Used parallel extraction agents and mechanical assembly to merge scattered README and tutorial files into standardized bilingual zh/en root directories README and TUTORIAL files. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. SSH remote port forwarding fails due to “address already in use” errors; subsequent rclone uploads timeout or fail on empty directories. Solution: Changed SSH configuration to a dynamic high port (10087) instead of a hardcoded low port. Refactored _rclone_upload for directory batch copying, and patched sync.py to treat missing sources as a skip rather than a fatal error.
Key Insight: Dynamic port selection is safer than static mapping in shared cluster environments; compared to individual file transfers, batch I/O reduces unstable tunnel overhead.
2. Claude Code repeatedly returns “not logged in” status across multiple sessions on TzJsDesktop, preventing any processing. Solution: Multiple login attempts failed; this requires manual CLI intervention or refreshing credentials outside the automated log range. No valid technical solution was found in session logs.
Key Insight: Continuous authentication errors hinder all AI-assisted workflows; manual verification of state management is necessary before automating complex tasks.
3. summarize CLI ignores the user-specified number of workers and hardcodes it as os.cpu_count(); additionally, rclone sync fails due to incorrect local and global configuration paths. Solution: Exposed --workers parameters in the parser and forwarded them via auto.py to daily.py. Created an application-specific ~/.config/summarize/config.json to correctly route LLM and rclone_remote settings.
Key Insight: CLI refactoring requires verifying parameter propagation across all intermediate script layers; application configuration usually requires distinct overrides different from system-level tool configurations.
4. All 43 batch merge sub-processes in summarize timeout due to LLM block limits and API rate limits under high concurrency; large files cause document assembly stagnation. Solution: Identified timeout as the root cause and began exploring local open-weight models (such as Qwen2.5) to reduce latency. Changed document integration to a mechanical process of “extracting then assembling” instead of single-generation generation.
Key Insight: High concurrency parallelism exposes API bottlenecks; separating semantic extraction from structural assembly can prevent LLM context limits from disrupting the batch document workflow.

Key insight: Multiple node.js installation methods (nvm and system npm) may cause global path conflicts; always verify the actual executed binary file.
5. Conda reported duplicate base environments on Windows because path string casing differed. Solution: Standardized string casing in environment registries.
Key insight: The Windows file system is case-insensitive, but many configuration parsers treat paths as case-sensitive strings, leading to logical duplicates.

Daily Report — 2026-06-27 Overview of Daily Work Completed Tasks: Performed A/B testing to improve the accuracy of visual instruction arrows generated by Cosmos3-Nano in robot demonstration videos. Implementation Methods: Modified inference parameters (standardized [0,1000] coordinates, scaled input to 480p, set temperature = 0), and implemented a simplified single-arrow visualization script for comparison tests. Results: Converted blurred model outputs into clear, actionable direction indicators, verified the model’s potential as a zero-sample annotator, and identified time constraints under static camera settings. Optimization of Cosmos3-Nano’s visual instruction generation through coordinate standardization, resolution scaling, and temperature control improved the qualitative usability of robot task annotations.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Visual instruction parameter optimization — Diagnosed coordinate misalignment and low resolution issues, then implemented three specific fixes: standardizing coordinates to [0,1000], scaling input to 480x480, and reducing temperature to 0 for deterministic output. Implementation and Fixes ✅ A/B testing execution — Ran base and improved configurations (successful and failed cases) on specific demonstration videos, downloaded results, and compared arrow orientation accuracy. ✅ Visualization simplification — Optimized output visualization to display only a single arrow, removing circular and multi-step indicators as requested by users. ✅ Server resource management — Downloaded all comparison assets to local storage and safely terminated Cosmos3-Nano vLLM service on remote servers to release GPU resources. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. AI-generated arrows were inaccurate and unevenly distributed because the model’s assumed image size (608x480) did not match the actual video resolution (256x256), coupled with the impact of low-resolution details. Solution: Implemented coordinate standardization to [0,1000] in the prompt, scaled input frames to 480p to better detect features, and set temperature to 0 to eliminate sampling noise.
Key Insight: These three modifications have independent value; coordinate standardization and resolution scaling are crucial for geometric accuracy, while temperature control ensures analytical certainty of temporal features.
General Issues 2. The remote vLLM process was not terminated initially due to a command-line mode mismatch (“vllm serve” matching the SSH command itself). Solution: Adjusted the pkill regular expression pattern to exclude the current shell environment (e.g., using “Cosmos3-Na[n]o”), successfully terminated the process, and released GPU resources.
Key Insight: When debugging remote processes, attention should be paid to regular expression patterns to avoid self-termination or incomplete termination.
Human and AI Approaches Implementation Level Visual Complexity Limitation Role Method Human Users explicitly requested simplified visualization (“only one arrow, no other content”) to reduce cognitive load and focus on direction intent. AI AI initially provided complex visualizations with multiple markers (circles, dots, step 1/2 arrows), which were then adjusted to a simplified form as required. Analysis of Differences: Humans clearly aim for clarity and simplicity, while AI defaults to maximum information density. Human intervention simplified evaluation metrics to focus solely on the geometric shape of the arrow.
AI Limitations Key Limitations AI incorrectly assumed video size (reported as 608x480, actual 256x256), leading to systematic coordinate distortion in early outputs. General Limitations Unable to demonstrate better temporal reasoning capabilities because the input video used is a static third-person camera, and frame-by-frame prediction tends to match segment-based predictions. Learning Outcomes Key Takeaways Using standardized coordinates (e.g., [0,1000]) in prompts significantly improves the geometric accuracy of VLMs with inconsistent internal image sizes. Practical Takeaways To isolate the impact of temporal context in video models, temperature must be set to 0 in ablation studies; otherwise, sampling noise obscures the true contribution of time segments. Key initiatives include: eliminating AI trust issues through strict audits; implementing secure multi-project DAG visualization using StatiCrypt to protect privacy; enhancing the DevCompanion workflow with flexible plan preview capabilities; fixing critical backend dependency issues in the Gadget translator. MacBook Completed the full lifecycle development of the cross-project Live DAG feature (UI optimization is planned); implemented DevCompanion plan visualization and skill deployment functions; packaged desktop video DMG files; conducted audits on AI behaviors to prevent virtual task execution. DCC Resolved disk quota issues by clearing pip cache, freeing space in HPC home directories. No significant activity in other areas. Severe AI hallucination issues and HPC infrastructure limitations were addressed; complex cross-project Live DAG feature was implemented for encrypted deployment; DevCompanion workflow plan visualization was optimized; the backend of the Gadget translator on Windows was stabilized.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Audit AI hallucinations in Phantom Tasks — By comparing git history with actual file system state, false commits and file creation behaviors related to weekly reports were investigated and dismissed, restoring workflow integrity. ✅ Implement cross-project Live DAG feature — A complete flow was achieved: registry (projects.json) → aggregator (aggregate-dag.ts) → overview renderer (render-overview.ts) → detail renderer (render-dag.ts extension) → encryption/deployment (build-dag-site.ts) → trigger (sync.py hook). Includes panoramic zoom and chart internal filtering UI. ✅ Implement plan visualization from ccplan→ccedit — By displaying complete executable functions at the end of ccplan (Phase 9) and start of ccedit, the DevCompanion workflow was enhanced. A relaxed parser was created for the review phase, solving type strictness issues between planning and execution phases. ✅ Fix Board bootstrap script on shared server — scripts/onboard-server.sh was refactored to support servers without sudo privileges, automatically discovers local AWS/Anthropic credentials, handles password-based SSH login, and forwards clones of private repositories via SSH proxy. ✅ Fix startup crash of translator application on Windows — PROXY_BYPASS was configured for localhost to resolve httpx proxy rejection issues. WeasyPrint/Marker dependency failures were addressed by replacing native PDF conversion with the standard library zipfile. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Deploy AI Companion skills into Claude and Codex — Modified skills (ccplan/ccedit) were linked to Claude via symbolic links; codex-setup.ts linked all six AI skills; PostToolUse hooks registered for Codex proxy environment. ✅ Package desktop video archives and DMG files — xcodebuild was used to generate Release archive (v5.0 Preview 0616); scripts/make-dmg.sh created distributable.dmg files with custom backgrounds and layouts. ✅ Local deployment of AI Companion skills — ai-companion skills were installed in the local user directory via symbolic links, resolving name conflicts with existing global skills in Claude Code and Codex. ✅ Build Gadget ECL Dagger framework — gadget.ecl.yaml was built from CLAUDE.md and git log, allowing overview display of two clusters (ai-companion and gadget) for local testing. ✅ Reproduce QueST model results — Reconstructed diagrams were aligned with the original QueST paper figures, ensuring correct labeling and comparison of method configurations (UNI2+HVG+STAIG). Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. AI compresses pseudo-results based on context, completing tasks that do not exist (weekly reports, new scripts, commits) rather than actual file system state. Solution: Direct CLI validation using git log, ls and file content checks to prove no changes. Present real data to AI so its operational context returns to reality.
Key Insight: Context compression may introduce persistent false user intentions across sessions; relying on external verification without AI summaries poses serious state discrepancy risks.
2. Conflict between “private deployment” requirements and “GitHub Pages public history”. A new private repository was proposed, but users rejected the expanded scope. Solution: Analyze existing infrastructure. It was found that Gadget source code is private, while only published pages are public. Client encryption using StatiCrypt was adopted; noindex/404 fallback was used to hide information. The “new repository” decision was abandoned.
Key Insight: Source code privacy does not equal deployment privacy. Client encryption on static hosting is a simple personal development tool pattern without complex infrastructure.
3. Gradio application crashes on Windows startup because environment proxy variables interfere with localhost health checks, and the lack of WeasyPrint/Marker dependency causes DOCX processing failure. Solution: PROXY_BYPASS=127.0.0.1 was explicitly set before server startup loop. core.py was refactored:.docx files containing zip files with word/document.xml are processed directly using Python standard library zipfile and xml.etree.ElementTree.
Key Insight: localhost should not pass through external proxies in network environments; environment variables must be programmatically overridden at startup. For structured formats like DOCX, avoiding a PDF intermediate layer on Windows is more robust.
General Issues 4. Bash script causes “unbound variable” error due to word splitting when passing empty optional parameters via SSH command line. Additionally, the exec engine fails validation due to working directory issues and lack of shell support. Solution: printf %q serialization was used instead of direct parameter passing to securely encode variables. ECL verify fields were actively fixed before execution; simple file existence tests replaced complex shell checks.
Key Insight: Complex string processing on remote shells requires careful escaping; using printf for secure variable transmission is safer than direct interpolation. The exec engine’s validation steps are vulnerable to environment context.
5. HPC home directory quota (25GB) is almost exhausted due to pip and datalab caches, blocking new operations. Solution: /hpc/home/zt81/.cache/pip was identified as the primary consumer (18GB), and python -m pip cache purge was executed; key model files were stored in .datalab.
Key Insight: In HPC systems with strict quotas, active and targeted cache management is crucial; knowing which caches can be re-downloaded and which require expensive model processing avoids unnecessary data loss.
6. Existing DAG YAML files lack “in progress” data, causing the overview to appear empty. Lack of “in progress” data also leads to incorrect state inference.Solution: A fallback UI was implemented: when no node is explicitly marked “in progress”, frontier_next (next available task) is displayed as a valid “in progress” indicator. CSS classDefs were updated to include in-progress. Status is obtained from the dependency graph rather than relying solely on explicit status flags. Key Insight: DAG visualization must handle sparse metadata gracefully; status is derived from the dependency graph rather than relying on explicit status flags.
7. Users repeatedly adjust UI layout: first “side panel”, then “internal chart overlay”. The initial implementation used page switching (render-dag style). Solution: render-overview.ts was refactored to support overlapping <div> layers filtered by a floating control panel within the same window. Mermaid works properly in hidden layers via “render then hide” mode.
Key Insight: User mental models of UI change during interaction. AI must clearly distinguish “page navigation” and “overlay filtering”, often requiring iterative adjustments to match user intent.
Human vs. AI Approaches Strategic Level Handling Phantom States in Workflows Role Approach Human Requires proof of action, asks “who made this?” and demands direct access to records/logs to verify intent; refuses to accept AI summaries as facts. AI AI confidently reports completed fictional tasks based on corrupted context summaries, treating hallucination constraints as valid user commands without verification. Analysis: Humans insist on audit trails of system states and real validation, revealing vulnerability when workflow scheduling relies solely on LLM-generated summaries.

Humans provide necessary boundary constraints (no repository split) leading to more pragmatic solutions.

AI AI focuses on optimizing zero-shot VLM integration and candidate selection technical plans, initially ignoring that verifying basic assumptions is more important than generating backends. AI Initially implemented multi-page navigation model (standard SPA mode). It was difficult to form a mental model of “overlay/filter” before clear feedback on location and behavior (“in the chart”). The difference highlights the importance of precise spatial description in UI requirements.

AI Limitations Key Limitations 1. AI compresses pseudo-results based on context, completing tasks that do not exist (weekly reports, new scripts, commits) rather than actual file system state. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Always use direct system commands to verify AI’s statements about state changes (files, commits); never trust text summaries of work completed in high-risk environments. The ECL/DevCompanion pipeline is very robust for complex functions; resolving topological issues via ccdiscuss before ccplan* can prevent large-scale replanning. When updating code in long-running background services, be sure to check the active PID via netstat before restarting; standard IDE reload methods do not apply to external child processes.
SSH proxy forwarding is a critical mode for securing git operations on temporary or restricted remote hosts. Understanding which caches can be re-downloaded and which require expensive processing can prevent unnecessary data loss in HPC systems. When designing deployment scripts for multi-user servers that do not require sudo, rely on user-space tools and SSH proxy forwarding. Solution: Implemented TypeScript adapter layer to standardize load; updated hook matcher; fixed Windows stdin BOM/TTY issues and removed outdated configuration items.
Key Insight: Different LLM clients use different internal architectures to handle tool execution hooks; a unified adapter layer is needed to support multiple proxies, with special attention to operating system-level input stream differences.
2. SlideshowController in Desktop Video suffers from observer leaks and security range errors during rapid video switching. Solution: Added explicit observer removal logic, fixed security range bookmark release timing, and repaired parallel review script execution using thunk instead of promises.
Key Insight: Event-driven UI requires strict observer lifecycle management; if promise objects are directly passed to functions expecting delayed calls, asynchronous workflow scripts often silently fail.
3. Ambiguity in spatial transcriptome results lies in whether the basic model (scGPT/TEDDY) is superior to traditional baselines. Solution: Aggregated ARI metrics by chapter, used a unified encoder to generate fair comparisons; confirmed “FM paradox”: the basic model performs well in cross-sample retrieval but worse in single-slide clustering compared to the original HVG.
Key Insight: The embedded basic model has unique advantages: superior in broad data understanding (retrieval), but inferior in local structure accuracy (clustering) compared to engineered baselines like HVG.
4. MuJoCo rendering degrades to CPU (llvmpipe) on Tianhe-2 only compute nodes, hindering evaluation. Solution: Installed NVIDIA GL/EGL user-space libraries in stages, configured glvnd supplier path to enable GPU rendering in containers lacking complete drivers.
Key Insight: Computing containers usually separate CUDA computation from OpenGL graphics; if the host driver version supports it, manually install user-space graphics libraries to achieve GPU rendering.
5. QueST training script crashes due to hard-coded batch size assumptions on small datasets. Solution: Checked source code, identified hardcoded logic, and repaired export scripts to explicitly set batch_num for two-slide operation.
Key Insight: Public science models typically contain implicit dataset size assumptions; source code inspection before integration is crucial to avoid crashes during small subset execution.
General Issues 6. Claude Code automatic skill installation failed due to invalid symbol link path placeholders. Solution: Fixed bash loop in symbol link generation script, removed invalid suffixes, and ensured valid file links.
Key Insight: Automated script generation may introduce minor string format errors; manual verification of file integrity after instantiation is essential.

Solution: Found HF_HOME directory configuration error causing token authentication bypass; fixed by exporting HF_TOKEN and verifying login status.Key Insight: Custom root directories typically change the credential lookup path; when performing authentication downloads in non-standard environments, explicit injection of environment variables is required.
Human and AI Approaches AI-Enhanced Hook Architecture and Execution Environment Role Approach Human Users clearly recognize the strategic need for dual agent support (Claude/Codex) and provide debugging constraints; manually refactor the UI of Desktop Video to prioritize user experience purity over traditional contract compliance. AI AI designs technical solutions: implement TypeScript adapters to standardize cross-platform architectures, diagnose Python/Node execution environments, and maintain architectural consistency of Desktop Video’s backend after UI changes. AI AI performs metric aggregation, visualization generation, and source code inspection. AI correctly identifies that FM ≈ training model in clustering, but differs in retrieval scenarios. Tianhe-2 Deployment and Resource Optimization | Role | Approach | |——|——| | Human | Despite version risks, users still use Cosmos3-Nano; initially thought it was necessary to reproduce the RoboCasa environment. | | AI | AI verified driver compatibility, identified existing labeled pi0.5 data (saving a lot of computation time), and resolved GPU rendering hardware limitations via lib staging. |
Difference Analysis: Humans accept architectural risks to pursue new models; AI optimizes resource usage by finding existing data and solving infrastructure obstacles, but users ensure strict benchmark matching requirements are met.
AI Limitations Key Limitations The first run of the adversarial review script failed because AI incorrectly passed a Promise object to the parallel execution helper instead of a Thunk function, resulting in silent failures during the validation phase. String sorting of version numbers during PyPI exploration was too simple, preventing detection of vllm 0.19.1 version. General Limitations Scripts patched via scp occasionally fail to execute due to intermittent SSH tunnel interruptions, leading to “no output” states, making direct state inspection difficult for debugging. Unable to independently resolve network bottlenecks (local Clash proxy); users need to intervene at home to restore upload speed of large model weights. Claude Code’s automatic generation of symbolic links contains string format errors (%/), requiring manual investigation and correction of bash logic. Initial PDF parsing cannot extract specific experimental settings of QueST; AI must manually inspect the text stream and metadata, rather than relying on direct PDF rendering. Lessons Learned Key Experiences The base model (scGPT/TEDDY) performs well in cross-sample niche retrieval, but is inferior to the original HVG in single slice clustering—this is a key finding in spatial transcriptome analysis. When using a hook system to support multiple LLM clients, rely on official SDK documentation to verify the tool_input structure, as their naming conventions and data formats often differ significantly. The Tianhe-2 A800 node can run CUDA 12.8 on 535 drivers (CUDA 12.2) via minor-version compatibility, confirmed by successful Torch matmul tests. Containerized HPC environments typically separate compute and graphics drivers; GPU rendering can be enabled on compute-only nodes without root privileges by locally installing the NVIDIA GL user space library. The async/await mode of the adversarial review script’s orchestration logic requires robust error handling; failing to encapsulate asynchronous calls as thunks may result in reports that appear “successful” or silent. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Mismatch of key intent: The evaluation code implemented the “EVALUATION.md” paper specification (CSR-RSR gap, single seed), which contradicts the authoritative “Panorama” summary (0–1 continuous recovery progress, multiple seeds), threatening experimental validity. Solution: Use multi-agent verification techniques to establish a complete record of intent and code, proving that “Panorama” is the true source; abandon the 500 steps/gap metric and replan evaluation to match SR + Bootstrap CI + RP.
Key insight: Technical documents (paper specifications) are often inconsistent with project high-level strategies; always verify code intent based on “Panorama” or execution summary first. Dead code in the framework layer should not be assumed to be active.
2. Failed results of Research Gadget LLM (timeout/rate limit) are permanently cached without TTL, causing subsequent runs to immediately return zero scores for all papers due to the same cache key. Solution: Found through workflow audit; the fix is to add a time-to-live (TTL) or unique request hash key to the cache entries in evaluate.py and insight.py to handle failed LLM responses.
Key insight: If the failed state and the successful state are identical in the cache without an expiration time, temporary API errors may lead to continuous data pollution. It is crucial to distinguish “temporary failure” and “permanent state” in the caching system.
3. Submitted files such as CLAUDE.md and settings.json expose absolute local paths (e.g., D:\GitHub\ai-companion), posing a risk of private path leakage. Solution: Implement three-layer fix: immediately use git rm –cached to delete existing exposed paths, update .gitignore to prevent future generation, and design installation programs with enhanced features to distinguish public and private visibility.
Key insight: Absolute paths in configuration files are essentially non-portable; treating them as “temporary” rather than “permanent” assets requires strict .gitignore implementation or environment variable injection.
General Issues 4. TokenMonitor displays new Anthropic models (such as Fable 5) as “unknown” without a token. Solution: Found that src-tauri/src/usage/pricing.rs lacks entries for specific new model IDs. The fix is to add these IDs to ModelFamily and update get_rates().
Key insight: Hard-coded pricing tables need strict maintenance to keep up with vendor releases; the fallback logic usually hides missing data points rather than indicating a need for updates.

Due to LLM rate limits, the sequential execution requirements of Research Gadget audit processes take over 30 minutes, making real-time auditing of very large code repositories slow. Absolute paths used in generated configuration files must be strictly excluded from the public repository; installation programs should detect repository visibility (public/private) and dynamically adjust inclusion strategies to prevent machine-specific local path leakage. Implementation: Achieved a strict “10 frames consecutive success” standard through adversarial testing; filtered and analyzed academic papers, proposed three hybrid architecture solutions; updated Rust standardization logic, added pricing indicators, and fixed the archive covering mechanism. Impact: Ensured effective benchmark metrics for recovery strategies, established a clear strategic path for JEPA-based robot perception, and guaranteed accurate billing and model identification in future Anthropic versions. Within two days, significant progress was made in terms of the rigor of Error Recovery’s benchmark evaluation, the integration of strategic literature in the JEPA robotics field, and the critical bug fixes for model pricing and data persistence in TokenMonitor applications.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ JEPA and Robotics Literature Analysis and Strategy — Filtered relevant papers (MemoryVLA++, iMaC, PRISM, etc.), conducted deep structural analysis, and proposed three implementable research directions combining hierarchical planning and event memory. ✅ Implementation of Error Recovery Benchmark Protocol — Unified the “10 frames consecutive success” standard for all evaluations, standardized the number of steps (500), and created adversarial unit tests to enforce protocol compliance. ✅ TokenMonitor Model Standardization and Pricing Fixes — Updated Rust logic to identify the Fable/Mythos model family, added pricing_available indicators, corrected official pricing standards, and fixed the cost rendering UI format. ✅ TokenMonitor Archive Data Persistence Fix — Modified the parsing logic to prioritize real-time logs over outdated hourly archives, preventing loss of new model data; reset the load caching usage. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Gadget Toolkit Documentation Maintenance — Reviewed and updated the root CLAUDE.md file in the Gadget repository to reflect the current architecture, MCP paths, and CLI interface. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. RecoverBench script uses “first frame success” logic, leading to exaggerated metrics and deviation from the documentation requirement of 10 frames consecutive. Solution: Implemented ConsecutiveSuccessTracker, first wrote L2 specification tests, then refactored all evaluation loops to enforce strict time limits.
Key Insight: Single-frame success validation severely overestimates reliability; strict time windows are crucial for accurate recovery rate calculation.
2. New Anthropic models appear “unknown” or “$0.00” due to standardization differences and outdated archive data covering real-time logs. Solution: Updated the new family’s normalize_model, added clear pricing indicators, and modified the parser logic to prioritize real-time log data over historical archives.
Key Insight: Without indicators, zero cost display cannot be distinguished from missing data; standardization fixes must be combined with cache invalidation to prevent historical data corruption.
3. Avoid expanding the scope during literature review by distinguishing video generation from robot control papers. Solution: Conduct strict filtering based on relevance to “robot perception, planning, and operation,” retaining only video papers that provide direct architectural inspiration for JEPA.
Key Insight: Potential spatial memory in diffusion models shares structural similarities with JEPA, allowing analogical architecture transfer across different fields.
General Issues 4. Research Scout pipeline timed out when processing a large batch of 100 LLM base filters. Solution: Refactored the pipeline, using smaller batches (50 papers) and increasing timeout thresholds to ensure reliable completion of JEPA/World Models search.
Key Insight: LLM tool calls have strict time limits; large-scale processing must be done in blocks to ensure reliability of long-term workflows.

Analysis of Differences: Humans identify business logic errors; AI executes technical fixes but lacks context about persistent layer interactions before being prompted.
AI Limitations General Limitations LLM tool calls via subprocess have strict time limits; large batch processing requires chunking for reliability, as shown in the Research Scout process. DLL/runtime issues in local Windows environment prevent actual Rust testing, forcing reliance on compilation validation. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Potential spatial interaction is a new trend in robot perception; V-JEPA’s potential space outperforms video diffusion baselines in intuitive physical modeling. Adopting “test first” approach (adversarial/unit tests) when aligning code and technical documentation is very effective, ensuring immediate compliance and avoiding regression issues. When fixing model normalization issues, always check the data persistence layer (archive/cache), as outdated historical data easily covers real-time improvements. Conducted a comprehensive multi-source audit of the RecoverBench project, and established a “test first, validate later” validation method to align discrepancies between documents, code, and experimental results.

Implementation and Fixes ✅ Creation of Prioritized Action List — Generated a prioritized Chinese action list, including immediate decisions (D1-D5), P0 fixes, and long-term reproducibility steps. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Title data (48.6%) does not match actual reproducible results; remote development file status is unclear. Solution: Used a parallel deep reader to map all sources, revealing that 48.6% are selected summary data, while a single checkpoint score is 45.7%; fully mapped the remote file structure on tianhe2.
Key Insight: Many “discrepancies” actually align code and data with each other, but deviate from the idealized paper; modifying code would destroy existing results, so documents must be adjusted to match the actual situation of the project.
General Issues 2. Missing background information about previous work, and audit documents are scattered across multiple repositories. Solution: Found the existing PAPER_VS_CODE_CONSISTENCY.md in the NIPS folder, reviewed its scope, and created a new integrated main document to avoid duplication while covering gaps in release integrity.
Key Insight: Fragmented documents make it easy to overlook critical differences; for reproducibility, unified sources are needed to identify these discrepancies.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Priorities of Testing and Fixing Role Method Human Humans explicitly stopped the immediate “code fix” phase, adhering to the “test first, validate later” principle, and prioritizing validation and specification definition before implementing changes. AI AI initially prepared direct code fixes and rerun plans; later started specific workflows to inventory existing tests and designed a three-tier testing framework. Discrepancy Analysis: Humans shifted strategy toward risk control and validation, ensuring “what we want to achieve” is clearly defined before action. AI transformed from direct fix execution into an analyst providing a structured validation framework.
Implementation Level Discrepancy Explanation Methods Role Method Human Humans tried to understand the actual state of the process and expected results, questioning the validity of existing assumptions. AI AI conducted comprehensive file system and code analysis to compare the real situation of the code repository with documents. Discrepancy Analysis: Humans focused on logical “reasons” and strategic consistency; AI provided detailed “content” through large-scale data synthesis, confirming qualitative arguments, but quantitative details are flawed.
AI Limitations General Constraints Initial SSH timeouts and directory mapping errors required iterative correction to find the correct remote development path on tianhe2. Workflow output is large (about 182KB), requiring custom Python scripts to extract concise summaries rather than reading directly. Learning Outcomes Key Takeaways In projects with complex discrepancies between documents, code, and experiments, “test first, validate later” is crucial: lock in current facts (feature validation tests) before attempting to align code with documents. Audit documents must cover release integrity and reproducibility bottlenecks, not just code and paper consistency, as missing resources render all results invalid. Impact: It was confirmed that TEDDY+Uni2 is the best-performing model in Visium HD, proving the fidelity of MIHD to the original STAIG algorithm. By supplierizing hooks/proTECTors, a clear “clone-and-use” strategy for AI Companion was established. Phased execution plans were used to protect the Gadget code repository, eliminating false positive errors to prevent unnecessary changes, and a low-risk cleanup was safely performed. DCC Completed Work: QueST jobs failed due to UnboundLocalError were fixed, HD experiments were rerun, and STAIG fusion consistency was verified. Architectural differences between the “gadget” workflow and “ai-companion” were analyzed to resolve portability conflicts. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: The full-process onboarding of the Gadget Python repository was executed, and migration strategies for AI Companion were analyzed. False positive error warnings in the parsing logic were eliminated. Implementation Methods: Python AST basics were used for inventorying, parallel Sonnet agents (subject to rate limits) were used for function classification, feature tests were written, and git-commit anchored analysis was performed on protector security. MIHD experimental results (QueST/HD) were restored and verified through STAIG consistency checks, a portable “supplier-level” architecture was designed to replace absolute path dependencies, the Gadget project underwent comprehensive code repository onboarding, a risk grading refactoring plan was generated, and architectural conflicts between traditional workflow tools and modern automated protectors were resolved.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Recovery and Verification of MIHD Results — UnboundLocalError in benchmark_rm_ideal.py was fixed, QueST and HD jobs were rerun, and encoder path accuracy was verified (PCA+Uni2 + ResNet50 performed best on DLPFC; TEDDY+Uni2 performed well on Visum HD). Approximately 2 months of lost code were restored via NetApp snapshots and git recovery. ✅ Onboarding of Gadget Project via /cconboard — Full-scale code repository onboarding was performed for the Gadget project (Phases 0–4, 7–8). A risk grading refactoring plan involving 667 items and ECL feature protectors were generated. Phase 5 was executed in stages to avoid interfering with unsubmitted changes. ✅ Verification of STAIG Fusion Consistency — Static and empirical comparisons were conducted between MIHD’s StaigFusionTrainer and the original STAIG. It was determined that identical outputs are impossible due to random generators, but consistency was verified through seed ARI/NMI comparison and isolated core validation. ✅ Portable Architecture Design for AI Companion — A “supplier-first” architecture was designed, replacing absolute path dependencies with local relative paths in ai-companion. Supplier-first tools (hooks, protectors, skills) are treated as relative path resources, while the heavy load engine is loaded externally but with delayed loading. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Gadget Code Cleanup (OB-515) — The redundant “import re as _re” in parsers.py was verified and fixed. Feature tests were written to lock behavior, the fix was applied, and 167 tests passed. ✅ Acceleration of HD Jobs — The 24-hour queue backlog problem for HD jobs was diagnosed and resolved, and the unavailable a6000 GPU was replaced with the available 5000Ada. ✅ Elimination of False Positive Errors in weekly_summary.py — Cases where ‘_cache_dir’ ignored ‘reports_dir’ were investigated. Cross-file grep and logical review confirmed that this was an intentional centralized caching design, not an error. No changes were made. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. AI Companion workflow suffers from portability issues due to absolute path injection. The parallel AI agent workflow encountered API rate limits (429 errors). Solution: A hybrid architecture was proposed: supplier-first tools are treated as relative paths, and the heavy load engine is externalized. Parallel LLM distribution was changed to a sequentially backend workflow subject to rate limits.
Key Insight: Absolute paths undermine portability; large-scale parallel LLMs require strict rate limits and real data provided manually to restore analytical quality in “phantom” projects.
2. The “pre-edition specification” protector conflicts with the existing ECL (DEC-004/001) regarding absolute path and self-authorization risks (BF-03). Solution: A threat model was analyzed: automated pre-edition protectors cannot rely on AI-generated states. A design was implemented where hooks prevent Claude editing, and git pre-commit anchors verify human intent.
Key Insight: Automated protectors must rely on immutable signals (git history) rather than internal flags to mitigate self-authorization attacks.
3. QueST jobs failed due to UnboundLocalError: ‘sections’ was used before assignment in benchmark_rm_ideal.py. HD Slurm jobs stalled for over 24 hours. Solution: Variable assignments were moved to the appropriate scope, and the job was rerun. The unavailable a6000 GPU was replaced with the available gc500Ada card via variant scripts.
Key Insight: Python variable scopes require strict sequential pre-assignment; if specific hardware types are strictly requested but unavailable, heterogeneous GPU partitions may cause deadlocks.
Human and AI Approaches GPU Partitioning and STAIG Consistency Design Role Approach Human Identified stalled HD jobs and requested regular GPU checks; suggested verifying STAIG consistency, but acknowledged that random generators make identical comparisons impossible. AI Queryed status of specific Slurm nodes to locate available 500Ada cards; transformed user consistency constraints into strict protocols using seed ARI/NMI and isolated core validation. Architecture Alignment and Gatekeeping Security Role Approach Human Identified that “human editing requires a record similar to git-commit” to address F-02 in automated gatekeeping. AI Integrated this insight into a two-layer system design (AI uses PreToolUse, humans use git pre-commit), and false positive errors were excluded through context consistency checks. AI Limitations General Limitations Initial Slurm GPU queries failed to distinguish total allocation from available GPU types, leading to inaccurate assessment of hardware combinations. AI initially marked _cache_dir as incorrect based on surface parameter usage, which was a false positive requiring deep context analysis for correction. Parallel AI agent workflows exceeded organizational API rate limits, resulting in incomplete analysis; initial function name queries were unreliable without clear context, producing “phantom” projects. Learning Outcomes Key Learnings MIHD’s StaigFusionTrainer is mathematically equivalent to the original STAIG under default paths; differences arise from n_clusters source code, not architectural issues. Merging the pipelines of AI Companion with the portable installation methods of gadget can resolve core conflicts. To make TypeScript CLI tools portable, reliance on supplier dependencies or npx-style parsing must be adopted. For large Python repositories, the /cconboard phased approach is highly effective, but if the work tree is dirty, pre-configured tests are required. Self-authorization attacks (BF-03) exist for “pre-edition specification” gatekeeping; gatekeeping must depend on external states (git/ask) rather than internal flags. Heterogeneous GPU partitions require precise node status diagnosis to avoid queue backlog. Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Git history rewrite optimization — Through targeted commits, removed unexpected Rust build files in TokenMonitor repository, saving approximately 302MB of space, while maintaining upstream synchronization and release tags. ✅ MIHD data recovery — Restored approximately two months of uncommitted work from NetApp snapshots, fixed critical errors in QueST/geneenc simulations, and resolved GPU scheduling starvation issues. ✅ Single-instance protection mechanism implementation — Developed a loop port locking mechanism for TokenMonitor Tauri application, including native dialogs and process detection logic across platforms to prevent duplicate instances at startup. ✅ aidev install CLI implementation — Created a CLI command supporting idempotency checks, platform-independent path standardization, and verification across five sibling repositories. 🔄 STAIG equivalence verification framework established — Designed and launched the verification framework to ensure the new ‘staig_fusion’ implementation is consistent with the original STAIG reference version while keeping ARI/NMI differences below 5%. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Approximately 302MB of accidentally committed build files damaged repository health; fully rewriting history might disrupt upstream synchronization. Solution: Identified specific违规 commits, only modified the ancestor commits, successfully reduced repository size, while maintaining a 0-behind status with upstream.
Key insight: When cleaning out forks, changing shared history alters ancestor SHAs; selective modification is more helpful for maintaining upstream relationships than broad filtering tools.
2. The “app is corrupted” error on macOS and potential duplicate instance conflicts were initially mistaken for port exhaustion or signature issues. Solution: Clarified that Tauri applications in production environments may not listen to ports, implemented synchronization and pre-event loop loop port locking with native dialogs, ensuring exclusive access and handling startup logic effectively.
Key insight: Cross-platform single-instance checks must be independent of the application event loop, considering both process existence and port occupancy for comprehensive verification.
3. aidev install failed idempotency checks due to inconsistent path separators (backslash vs slash) and text differences in markers across platforms. Solution: Implemented fuzzy matching for markers and normalized path processing before comparison, adding pre-flight verification steps to ensure consistent state detection.
Key insight: Cross-platform CLI tools must standardize separators and check target states, not just file existence, to ensure true idempotency.
4. MIHD Slurm jobs fell into PD state; TokenMonitor showed blank screen due to isolated Vite port; QueST scripts produced UnboundLocalError. Solution: Resolved GPU scheduling starvation by switching device types, cleaned up zombie processes to establish normal port binding, and fixed variable scope issues in benchmark scripts.
Key insight: In HPC, specific hardware constraints often hinder jobs more than partition priorities; if zombie processes persist after a development server crash, Tauri’s strict port mode will silently fail.

AI AI initially tried the full filter-repo, causing upstream synchronization interruption; turned to targeted modifications after users identified an “behind” status anomaly. When verifying scientific code equivalence across different environments, always use final output metrics (such as ARI/NMI) as the basis for verification, rather than trying to achieve identical reproducibility. Tauri applications in production may not listen to ports at startup; single-instance logic must be synchronized and independent of the application event loop to operate reliably. Key Insight: Updater signature (minisign) and code signing (Apple) are distinct; mixing them together disrupts cross-platform update consistency. Clean Base64-encrypted key pairs are essential for Tauri workflows.

AI Limitations General Limitations If not wrapped in try/catch, LLM-wrapped implementations often crash during timeout, easily confused with JSON parsing errors; this is common in many projects today. Dependence on file metadata (dates/logs) rather than binary content (md5sums) initially masked the severity of data corruption in MIHD; explicit artifact verification is needed to prove byte-level identity errors. Unable to predict local environment differences (python3 vs python, Tauri key formats) causes CI/publish script failures, requiring manual iteration of secret formats and scripts. System snapshots are important security measures but cannot replace version control. Root tsconfig in a workspace should often be set to “pure reference” (include: []) to avoid CommonJS/ESM parsing conflicts that cause build failures. Practical Lessons Tauri updater signature (minisign) and code signing (Apple/DigiCert) are independent; mixing them in CI workflows disrupts automatic update consistency across platforms. Switched to shell=False and verified through direct subprocess testing. ✅ Resolved main interface cost display and cache latency issues — Investigated why “Device Cost” exists in “DevicesView” but is missing from the main “App.svelte” interface; disk cache latency was identified as the root cause. clear_prefix was implemented in SSH sync and usage view update functions to prevent old data retrieval. ✅ Implemented native session context — Replaced manual prompt injection history mechanisms with the native --resume/--session-id features of Claude CLI. All adapters (Claude, Codex, Gemini) were updated to pass user IDs for session isolation. ✅ Integrated launcher entry points — Created launcher.py as a single source of truth for server startup logic (pre-check, PID management, port binding).start.bat, start.ps1, and start.sh were refactored to handle only the thin wrapper for conda activation. The aggregation logic was modified to rely on enabled status rather than independent flags. ✅ Restored optimization and conversion — Reviewed and optimized the recovery content in CVPR network sections, focusing on narrative structure and author format. After installing necessary dependencies, resume.md was converted to resume.docx using python-docx. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. The main interface of TokenMonitor displays outdated costs because the disk cache is never cleared after SSH sync, only the memory cache is emptied. Solution: Added disk_cache.clear_prefix("usage-view:") calls in sync_ssh_host, clear_usage_view_cache, and the background SSH sync loop to ensure latest data is recalculated always. Confirmed that although previously concerned about “Tianhe” device records, no original data loss occurred.
Key Insight: In a persistent desktop environment like Tauri, simultaneous destruction of state in one layer (memory cache) and another layer (disk cache) leads to inconsistent views; both must be synchronized during invalidation.
2. Claude CLI continues to timeout (120 seconds) when handling complex calendar requests with no output, due to shell=True on Windows causing stdio deadlock when generating sub-MCP processes. Solution: It was found that inherited pipeline processing causes hidden deadlocks. By setting shell=False in subprocess calls and using native session persistence (--resume) to manage context, reliable execution and memory retention are ensured.
Key Insight: Popen and subprocess inheritance in Windows cmd.exe behavior may cause hidden stdio deadlocks that are invisible in advanced logs; empirical isolation testing is needed to determine the cause.
General Issues 3. Multiple ways to start servers in LifeCopilot lead to configuration drift, and new SSH devices in TokenMonitor have default exclusion statistics due to mismatched configurations. Solution: All pre-check logic was centralized in launcher.py for LifeCopilot. Standardized default flags in the Rust/TS layer of TokenMonitor to ensure “connected” devices are automatically included in cost reports, unless explicitly excluded.
Key Insight: Configuration management should be encoded as a single executable script or unified storage, rather than decentralized management, to reduce cognitive load and prevent configuration drift.

In TokenMonitor, users provide visual comparisons of cost differences to break ambiguity during debugging. Analysis of Differences: Humans prioritize empirical validation over theoretical explanations, forcing AI to verify hypotheses through direct system interaction and visual data correlation, rather than relying solely on code logic analysis.

AI The AI identified and implemented --resume/--session-id support across all adapters, and correctly deduced the reason for disk cache failure in persistent Tauri processes after being confused by changes within memory. Analysis of Differences: Users defined high-level architectural requirements (native sessions, persistence awareness); AI executed implementation details and system-specific optimizations.
AI Limitations Key Limitations 3. Multiple ways to start servers in LifeCopilot lead to configuration drift, and new SSH devices in TokenMonitor have default exclusion statistics due to mismatched configurations. - Initially guessed the root cause of CLI timeout errors and was confused by Tauri persistence mechanisms, failing to realize that disk cache clearing was also required beyond memory cache fixes. Failed to immediately recognize shell=True causing stdio and subprocess deadlock on Windows, requiring extensive manual testing and visual evidence from users to locate the issue. Lessons Learned Key Experiences On Windows, simultaneously starting subprocess.Popen and shell=True to generate their own subprocesses (e.g., MCP servers) may cause stdio deadlock due to handle inheritance. Avoid shell=True unless absolutely necessary for command parsing. In Tauri/desktop applications, always clear both disk cache and memory cache when state changes to prevent old data leakage; remote sync caches are invalid and cannot be persisted. Practical Experience When debugging CLI tools or UI anomalies, always verify the original payload and cache keys through visual evidence to distinguish the cache layer from computational logic, rather than relying solely on code tracing. Problems and Solutions General Issues 1. AI JSON parsing fails when the model generates distorted or truncated JSON structures due to complex prompts. Solution: Users provide clear repair instructions; AI corrects the structure. Later, prompts are simplified to ensure a stable output format.
Key Insight: Complex prompt engineering requires iterative validation of output patterns to prevent silent generation errors.

Solution: Use optimized search queries containing specific robotics terms (“visual-motion strategy”, “action chunking”, “TinyVLA”) and use targeted scripts to filter relevant arXiv categories.
Key Insight: Domain-specific keyword filtering is crucial for relevance retrieval; generic machine learning terms usually return irrelevant computer vision results.

Daily Report — 2026-05-20 General Overview Completed work: Reviewed the proxy workflow protocol in the TokenMonitor repository along with the current code base and configuration files. Implementation: Executed shell commands to check file structures, track Python module imports, and verify hook behavior, without modifying source code. Impact: Identified major flaws in the “standard execution” mechanism due to naming conflicts with sister repositories and inaccurate documentation. A protocol review of TokenMonitor revealed significant differences between the documentation claims and actual implementation in standard execution and Python import parsing.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Protocol verification review — Confirmed whether the statements in AGENTS.md align with the actual implementation of the verification gate and specification management scripts. ✅ Hook behavior verification — Tested the execution paths of check_spec.py and verify.py to ensure they operate correctly according to the defined workflow. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. AGENTS.md claims hooks execute “verification + review”, but .claude/settings.json only triggers verification, resulting in the review generation not being enforced. Solution: Found missing hook configuration; suggested adding the call to review_generator to Stop hooks (if necessary).
Key insight: Documentation often overstates the protection mechanisms implemented; clear configuration reviews are needed to ensure accuracy.
2. Running python workflow/verify.py directly caused import errors, pulling code from sister repository D:\GitHub\gadget rather than TokenMonitor. Solution: Switch to python -m workflow.verify, which can correctly parse modules within the TokenMonitor context.
Key insight: If no virtual environment or strict path isolation is used, sister repositories with the same package structure pose a hidden import hijacking risk.
General Issues 3. Documentation claims python workflow/active_spec.py generates specifications, but it is a library file that does not produce side effects. Solution: Clearly state that the file contains only logic; a CLI wrapper or explicit API usage instructions are required.
Key insight: Library scripts usually lack entry point logic; assuming they are runnable CLIs leads to operational dead ends.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Accuracy Analysis of Documentation Role Method Human No request for checking outdated specifications or import paths. AI The AI inferred that missing combined successful verification runs of active-spec.json indicate a virtual import source, thus identifying the repository conflict in gadget. Analysis difference: The AI identified a critical architectural flaw (outdated specifications allow writing), which stems from environment isolation issues, while typical text reviews ignore this issue.
Import Parsing Debugging Role Method Human User asked a vague question “check if it’s correct”, relying on the AI to determine scope and depth. AI The AI autonomously decided to check shell output, track imports via sys.path, and compare documentation with runtime behavior. Analysis difference: The AI demonstrated deep diagnostic capabilities, able to detect brother repository hijacking issues that require understanding Python import priority rules, rather than just simple text search.
AI Limitations General Limitations The initial shell command failed due to mismatched context path (located in D:\Github instead of TokenMonitor), requiring iterative correction. The AI initially had parsing errors when handling JSON input here-string syntax in PowerShell, before switching to variables. Lessons Learned Key Experiences When auditing multi-repository workspaces, always verify Python import sources through sys.path and __file__ to prevent cross-contamination. Practical Experience Ensure the test environment dependencies (e.g., pytest) exist before running verification scripts that depend on them. 2. After completion, automatically runs verification: pass proceeds to review, fail pauses into debug mode with structured hypotheses.
3. PyTorch CUDA packages (torch+cu130, torchvision+cu130) not available on standard PyPI causing pip installation failures [Conda Environment Migration] (2026-05-11) Solution: Added –extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 to pip dependency sections in all yml files to access PyTorch’s CUDA-specific package index.
4. 5. 6. Missing cross-session context recording preventing next session or other agents from knowing what was done and why [Unified Agentic Workflow System] (2026-05-11) Solution: Implemented dual-format review logs: human version .md (narrative suitable for review/PR descriptions) and agent version .agent.json (structured JSON with files_modified, rationale, reasoning_chain for program reading).
7. 8. GitHub Pages website not updating despite local builds succeeding - update.sh Step 9 silently failing [Summarize Deployment Pipeline] (2026-05-12) Solution: Re-cloned tzj2006.github.io repository into website/public/ directory after discovering it lacked independent .git, fixing silent push operation failures.
Learnings Architecture (architecture) Structured specs with mandatory fields (Goal, Scope, Constraints, Success Criteria, Non-goals) prevent AI misunderstanding better than natural language prompts. Success criteria should be executable definitions of ‘what success looks like’ - conceptually identical to verification gates, not separate steps. Community mature tools (Spec Kit 95K stars, Entire CLI 4.3K stars, git-cliff 11.8K stars) are more reliable through large-scale validation than custom builds. Prioritize adoption, only build custom for gaps (like debug mode) and glue layer (like AGENTS.md protocol). Cross-session context transfer needs dual format: human version (narrative, suitable for review/PR) and agent version (structured JSON, suitable for program reading). Single format cannot serve both needs. Recording original plan in review log enables ‘intent vs result’ comparison for reflection and improvement. Subagent-Driven Development excels at parallel execution of independent tasks: dispatch fresh subagent for each task (independent context), do two-stage review after completion (spec compliance → code quality), avoiding main session context pollution. AGENTS.md as cross-agent protocol is more universal than SKILL.md, readable by Codex/Cursor/Claude/Copilot. .cursorrules is Cursor-specific supplement - combining both covers all agents. Debugging (debugging) AI’s all judgments must have transparent reasoning chains (‘because X → therefore Y’ with evidence and confidence levels). Pausing for user confirmation on failure is more efficient than blind retries. Structured hypotheses force AI to make reasoning explicit. When debugging deployment pipelines, verify the entire infrastructure chain (code logic + file paths + git repos + remote endpoints), not just code logic. AI can find code bugs but may miss infrastructure-layer issues without end-to-end verification. Gitignored directories that should be independent git submodules need explicit verification during debugging. Absence of .git in expected locations is a critical diagnostic signal for silent deployment failures. Domain Knowledge (domain) PyTorch CUDA packages require explicit index URL configuration (–extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130). Standard PyPI only hosts CPU versions, and +cu130 version strings will fail pip resolution. Tools (tools) Conda environment migration with mixed conda/pip dependencies is fragile. Two-phase approach (conda packages first, then pip separately with error tolerance) provides more control and recovery options than integrated conda env create. Source-installed packages need manual exclusion and reinstallation. Windows path manipulation in bash/sed is error-prone due to backslash escaping complexity. For complex string replacements, delegating to native PowerShell commands (Get-Content | .Replace() | Set-Content) is more reliable. AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Subagent-Driven Development for parallel independent tasks with isolated contexts ✓ Dual-format review logs (human .md + agent .json) for cross-session context transfer ✓ Structured hypothesis reasoning in debug mode forcing transparent ‘because→therefore’ chains ✓ Root cause analysis through systematic code tracing combined with infrastructure verification ✓ Two-phase problem solving: identify code bugs first, then verify infrastructure layer Limitations:
✗ Background task outputs (run_in_background: true) frequently truncated or lost, requiring fallback to foreground execution ✗ Initially underestimated community tool maturity, leaned toward custom build for control rather than prioritizing proven solutions ✗ Tendency toward over-layered design, splitting conceptually unified concepts into separate independent components ✗ Initial debugging focused only on code logic layer, missed infrastructure issues (missing git repos) until prompted by human observation of actual deployment state ✗ Did not proactively verify end-to-end deployment path before declaring fixes complete ✗ Didn’t proactively include original plan in review logs for intent vs result comparison Next Week Outlook Monitor Unified Agentic Workflow system in production across three repositories, iterating based on real-world usage patterns and edge cases. Continue refining summarize deployment pipeline to handle any remaining edge cases discovered during backlog processing. Potential focus areas: workflow system documentation improvements, additional test coverage for deployment edge cases, and evaluation of whether workflow patterns should be extended to other repositories in the ecosystem.
