GTK bottom-up size negotiation causes FloatBall window to always be 400x400, Tauri set_size() is completely ineffective [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-04) Solution: Use the with_webview() callback to call widget.set_size_request() in the GTK main thread, breaking theWebKitGTK natural size constraint. Remove the set_resizable switch (with_webview is asynchronous, subsequent API calls will be queued before the callback execution, locking the old size). Keep resizable enabled permanently on Linux
2. Dynamic resize of Linux transparent borderless window causes systematic WM +305px/+113px position offset, probe/corrective mechanisms cause visible flickering, size inconsistency between WebView and native window [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-05) Solution: Architectural refactoring to a fixed expanded size window + GDK input_shape_combine_region: Only the ball area (56×56) accepts events when collapsed; the whole window accepts events during expansion and dragging. Completely eliminates resize operations. Remove 150 lines of patch code
3. On Linux/Wayland, Tauri main window set_position() is completely ignored by the compositor, causing the window to appear in the center of the screen [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Detect WAYLAND_DISPLAY at the run() entry point and force GDK_BACKEND=x11, enabling the application to run via XWayland, bypassing the fundamental limitation of the Wayland protocol prohibiting client absolute position settings
4. In ssh_remote.rs, assert!() panics the entire program when path validation fails, provider parameters not validated allow path traversal attacks [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Change the function signature to Result<PathBuf, String>, using? for error propagation;Add a whitelist function validate_provider() (only allowing ‘claude’ and ‘codex’).
5. sync_ssh_host blocks all readers when holding a RwLock read lock during an SSH I/O await point that lasts several seconds [TokenMonitor] (2026-04-02) Solution: Add #[derive(Clone)] to SshCacheManager to clone the manager before await and release the lock in advance.
6. The three-layer architecture of Life-Copilot MCP services is broken simultaneously: FastMCP does not call run(), mcp_servers.json is missing, and Butler commands are never passed to the Claude CLI child process [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04)Solutions: Create main.py to start the stdio transport; create.claude/mcp_servers.json; ClaudeAdapter adds –append-system-prompt parameter; simultaneously create convention files (AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) for Codex/Gemini, and all 19 MCP tools are restored. 7. 8. ClaudeCLIAdapter.is_available() lacks async and await synchronous methods cause TypeError, which is silently ignored by except Exception, resulting in Claude being silently downgraded to Codex and timeout [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Add the async keyword, and Claude available: True returns to normal. Synchronous fix for context loss during multiple rounds of dialogue (_process_input never passes last_assistant_message and last_intent parameters).
9. The initial solution for Linux Screen Time Tracker uses xdotool, but the user’s Wayland environment (GNOME) is completely unavailable [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Switch to GNOME Introspect D-Bus (org.gnome.Shell.Introspect.GetWindows()) as the main path, use xprop as a XWayland fallback, and use PID→cmdline as the final fallback. All subprocess calls add a 5-second timeout + proc.kill(). This issue was actively discovered by Critic subagent adversarial review.

Also identify that the skip_completed mechanism in the pipeline cannot detect structural defects in invalid content.
12. Leiden clustering cannot accurately match n_clusters, limited by fair comparison with KMeans [MIHD] (2026-03-31) Solution: Implement a binary search in cluster_with_leiden(): perform up to 20 iterations of adjustment on resolution within [0.01, 10] range until the number of clusters matches, using the monotonic relationship between resolution and number of clusters for efficient convergence.
13. lark-oapi WebSocket client runs blockingly, Client.start() conflicts with FastAPI asyncio main loop [Life-Copilot] (2026-04-04) Solution: Start the Feishu bot in a separate daemon thread, and use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe() to bridge message callbacks to the main event loop. This issue was pre-discovered by Critic subagent adversarial review.
Learning Insights Architecture The correct architecture for Linux transparent borderless Tauri/WebKitGTK floating windows is a fixed large-native window + internal pure CSS expansion/collapse, without relying on frequent resize of the outer window. GTK bottom-up negotiation takes max(window_requested, widget_natural_size); the with_webview() callback must call widget.set_size_request() to break theWebKitGTK natural size constraint; dimensions and positions of content areas in WM, GTK, and WebView do not sync automatically—this is platform constraint, not a bug. The Wayland protocol prohibits client-controlled absolute window position at the design level; any set_position() retry strategy is ineffective. The correct solution is to detect WAYLAND_DISPLAY and force GDK_BACKEND=x11 to fallback to XWayland. X11 WM will force the undecorated window into the visible area, and the edge offset varies by platform (Linux edge_offset=0, macOS/Windows can be half-screen). Aggressive simplification is often more effective than incremental fixes: the Thin Adapter+MCP Server+Skills three-layer model replaces the 3170-line proprietary routing logic, removing 2823 lines and achieving cross-CLI generality. Multi-CLI systems should use convention files (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) rather than runtime injection; unifying the history ring buffer is more reliable than adapting to each CLI session mechanism. The complete MCP configuration for Claude CLI -p non-interactive mode requires two steps: (1) explicitly pass –mcp-config to load project-level tools; (2) add –permission-mode bypassPermissions to bypass permission confirmation. The wildcard in –allowedTools is unreliable in this mode due to contention with MCP server initialization, and bypassPermissions is the correct pattern for backend service calls. Debugging Runtime logs are the fundamental means of underlying system debugging: when underlying system behaviors such as GTK, WM, or OS occur, priority should be given to verification through logs/monitors (e.g., backend.log shows +305px systematic offset) rather than inference from code. After multiple failed fixes, identify the boundary where “continuing fixes cannot solve architectural issues” and stop local fixes to focus on root cause analysis. “Parameters are implemented in code” does not mean “parameters are passed”: the integration layer is the most common connection break point; verify by checking the calling side rather than just the implementation side. In Python, synchronous await methods cause TypeError; if silently caught by except Exception, it leads to silent functionality downgrade instead of an error, making troubleshooting difficult. When debugging nested process CLI tools (main process→Claude CLI→MCP server), record actual command-line parameters first and then isolate each parameter to verify its effect, which is more efficient than guessing parameter behavior directly. The skip_completed mechanism in the pipeline cannot detect files with invalid content (all gt_labels are -1); active verification of content validity is required. Tools The divergent exploration of ccplan skills (multiple solutions) + Critic adversarial review + feasibility probing process can effectively transform complex platform architecture issues into executable plans. During this week’s Critic phase, high-value issues such as Wayland compatibility, lark-oapi thread blocking, ThoughtStore not being a singleton, and 4 hidden code dependencies were pre-discovered, offering high ROI and serving as key engineering practices for handling high uncertainty tasks. GDK input_shape_combine_region intercepts events at the X11 layer; setPointerCapture cannot bypass it. In drag scenarios, input shape should be temporarily extended to the full window on the Rust side. GTK’s resizable(false) WM hint prevents both user dragging and programmatic set_size(), and dynamic size adjustment requires temporary unlocking. assert!() and unwrap() in Rust production code are potential crash points when accepting external inputs; uniformly change to Result and use? for propagation. Lock cross-await points are common risks in asynchronous programming; the solution is to Clone the required data before await to release the lock in advance. Any user input concatenated into a file path must be validated via a whitelist (more reliable than a blacklist). When wrapping stdlib logging with structlog, explicitly add ExtraAdder() processor; otherwise, the extra={} field silently disappears without error. git reset –soft is an efficient way to organize commit history, allowing any number of commits to be compressed into semantically clear commits, suitable for CI environments and automation tools. Domain Knowledge Core MIHD experiment conclusion: High-quality embeddings are more important than clustering method selection (STAIG+mclust ARI=0.546 vs STAIG+Leiden=0.513); the STAIG fusion framework is highly robust to gene encoders (Teddy ARI=0.495 vs PCA ARI=0.497); the space graph contrast learning mechanism dominates clustering performance, and the impact of gene embedding quality is greatly diluted. Foundation Models suffer from systematic transfer loss in cross-domain downstream tasks (Teddy gene-only ARI=0.186 is inferior to PCA=0.255; optimization goals do not match); HD dimension imbalance issues (concatenation of 1586d=50d PCA+1536d UNI2 is worse than single modality); data scale is a key variable (adaln is effective in DLPFC but completely fails in HD 17502 spots). The narrative of multimodal fusion papers should equally emphasize negative and positive results. The paper setting should define research gaps (“no system study on zero-shot FM fusion currently exists”) rather than method performance; claiming single modality can also perform retrieval adds stronger argumentation by including this rebuttal (simple fusion is a trap→space graph learning is the bridge→correct fusion can surpass single modality). NeurIPS D&B Track submission strategy: “domain correctors” (quantifying specific benchmark defects) are more accepted than “new method proposers”; reviewers value multi-dimensional evaluation, fair baseline comparisons, manual verification mechanisms (κ≥0.68), and counterintuitive negative findings. Nature Methods Analysis level requires each method to run 10 times with mean±std and 4-dimensional evaluation. Modern Linux desktops (Ubuntu 22.04+) default to Wayland; cross-platform window tracking should use GNOME Introspect D-Bus as the main path, with xdotool/xprop only as XWayland fallback. Background sampling tasks should not rely on CronScheduler with a minimum tick of 60s; non-minute interval tasks require independent asyncio.Task loop. AI Usage Notes Effective Modes:
✓ Critic subagent adversarial review: actively discovers high-value architectural risks such as Wayland compatibility, lark-oapi thread blocking, ThoughtStore not being a singleton, and 4 hidden code dependencies during planning, avoiding large-scale rework later and being key to successful delivery of multiple projects this week. ✓ Parallel subagents generate code in batches: create multiple analysis scripts (cross-slice Query aggregation, Fig visualization, HD Marker Gene visualization) simultaneously, significantly reducing serial processing time for multiple tasks. ✓ Systematic multi-layer troubleshooting: start from log evidence (+305px offset in backend.log, permission_denials field) and confirm assumptions layer by layer to locate the root cause, showing strength in complex issues such as MCP three-layer breakage and GTK size negotiation. ✓ ccplan structured planning breaks complex platform issues like FloatBall Linux fixes into 6 alternatives, and converges on the optimal solution after feasibility probing. ✓ ECL documentation persistence across sessions: during multiple days of continuous FloatBall fixes, use /compact to restore context, reducing repeated analysis costs.Limitations: ✗ When no running environment is available, incorrect assumptions were made that the underlying APIs (Tauri set_size, GTK gravity, Google Calendar calendarList scope) work as expected. Multiple iterations of fixes were carried out at the wrong level, and direction needs to be corrected through user testing feedback or log evidence. ✗ After multiple rounds of fixing attempts, the system failed to actively identify the boundary that “continuing patching cannot resolve architectural issues”. Every time new logs appeared, another solution was tried. Root cause analysis only occurs upon explicit user request. ✗ Outdated or fabricated information was provided in the fast-iteration product area (AionUI slash commands, Claude context window specifications). Technical parameters updated rapidly should not be stated in a definitive tone. ✗ Lack of local environment awareness: It defaults to cloning repositories already present locally from GitHub instead of prioritizing search in the local file system. ✗ Mistake in judgment of git operation scope: When users requested “rolling back changes in this session”, git stash was used incorrectly, affecting all uncommitted changes and nearly causing loss of historical work. ✗ Incomplete awareness of global dependencies in large code repositories. Issues such as broken connections in the integration layer (parameters not passed) require multiple rounds of investigation to be identified. Next Week’s Plan Four key areas for next week: (1) MIHD paper — collect the complete HD evaluation table for basic_contrastive HD experiments, advance the code gap tasks (Leiden result restoration script, figure generation script, spatial continuity metrics, multi-seed support), start paper figure generation and draft writing, with the goal of reaching a submitable draft level; (2) TokenMonitor — finally verify the fixed window + GDK Input Shape solution on real Linux devices, confirm that the WM clamp issue is resolved. If verified, a PR will be merged, and the Linux FloatBall fix will be completed, ending this long-running task that has lasted nearly two weeks; (3) Life-Copilot — obtain OpenReview account credentials to unlock the NeurIPS review feedback function, verify the stability of Screen Time Tracker in production environments, and continuously observe the performance of the 11-level fallback chain in real use; (4) Research exploration — convert the conclusions of the NeurIPS D&B Track survey into specific experimental designs, evaluate the feasibility of a multi-dimensional evaluation benchmark for VLM credibility, and follow up on the AionUI remote SSH access feature request.

Solution: Design fixed-window benchmarks, dynamically expand the click area only during dragging via RPC, completely bypassing WM resize functions instead of fixing symptom loops.
Key Insight: Platform geometric mismatch is an architectural fault; dynamic interaction boundaries should be driven by state, not staticly bound to component size.
2. Remote operation success threshold accepted physically unstable states, while the data pipeline silently fallback to mismatched dataset paths, and state files (.npz) differed significantly between macOS ARM and Linux x86_64 environments. Solution: Replace static coordinate checks with continuous frame stability counters and mandatory physical release verification; completely rewrite the environment registry loader to implement strict failure mechanisms for fingerprint mismatches; treat MuJoCo constraint solver differences as hardware-level floating-point accumulation issues. Key Insight: Floating-point physical simulation requires dynamic physical state verification, not position threshold detection; silent default configurations always destroy data integrity regardless of process completion.
3. Copied Crossformer and LiPM metrics differed significantly from published papers, despite correct architectural implementation, indicating programmed anomalies rather than code defects. Solution: Generate diagnostic scripts to simulate unit scaling, loss function changes, and aggregation methods; verify MAE ≤ RMSE relationship under sample-average processes; develop structured technical inquiry templates for direct author verification.
Key Insight: Published academic metrics often violate basic mathematical inequalities or contain unrecorded preprocessing steps; systematic scenario mapping is more effective at identifying methodological flaws than blind re-training.
4. Claude CLI -p mode silently rejected MCP tools with authorization bypass and ignored local project configurations, while default JSON serialization of structlog discarded stdlib extra upper and lower text fields, causing critical robot dialogue logs to be truncated. Solution: Inject explicit configuration flags and bypassPermissions mode into the CLI adapter, integrate custom structlog processor to explicitly convert opaque context buckets into final JSON data.
Key Insight: Headless AI agents enforce strict interaction boundaries and require explicit bypass flags; serialization frameworks discard non-native dictionaries unless explicitly merged during process execution.
5. Large model initialization caused subprocess pipeline deadlock and socket timeouts during parallel VLA server startup, causing inference requests to be discarded before warm-up completion. Solution: Redirect heavy stdout/stderr to direct file streams, expand connection timeout to accommodate JIT compilation phase, inject explicit warm-up calls before batch cycles, and implement fault-isolation GPU scheduling.
Key Insight: ML infrastructure I/O pipelines must separate connection establishment from computation warm-up; standard buffer limits cannot safely handle kilobyte-level model loading outputs.

Heavy I/O operations in ML infrastructure (model loading, context transfer) require explicit buffer management, out-of-band logging mechanisms, and JIT-aware socket timeout configurations to prevent initialization deadlock and connection state corruption. Academic metric differences usually stem from unrecorded preprocessing, unit normalization errors, or structural symbol violations, not architectural flaws; hypothesis-driven scenario mapping is more effective at isolating faults than blind re-training. Data corruption in benchmark tests (missing NPZ metadata), infinite recursion risk in successful checks, failure of action deformation across scenarios, and parallel EGL deadlocks hindered verification and enhancement. Key Insight: Metadata collection must survive the serialization round-trip; using only manifest tags cannot guarantee the success or remote verification readiness of physics-based policies, which need confirmation via empirical deployment verification mechanisms before training preparation.
2. Dependency conflicts across environments, asynchronous signature mismatches, and silent fallback timeouts disrupted pipeline execution and provider routing. Solution: Implemented clear virtual environment goal setting, performed strict linting/type checking at chain initialization, corrected asynchronous method declarations, and bypassed Shell buffer to ensure stable toolchain parsing. Key Insight: Resolving dependency issues in multi-language environments requires explicit environment goal specification; unhandled adapter chains with asynchronous mismatches cause implicit exceptions to be swallowed, which must be captured during initialization rather than runtime.
3. External API authentication restrictions (OpenReview 403) and implicit failures of provider keys disrupted automated research workflows and data collection pipelines. Solution: Recorded boundary constraints, shifted to analysis using only metadata, built key_validator.py with real-time OAuth scope verification, and set error logs to WARNING/ERROR to display status banners.
Key Insight: When authentication fails, resilient research tools must gracefully degrade; token verification must distinguish file existence, scope boundaries, and real-time API accessibility to prevent misjudgment.
4. Fragmented CLI session states, missing context injection, and loss of multi-round history led to hallucinations in proxies and routing failures between different backends. Solution: Deployed a lightweight prompt injection history ring buffer, migrated MCP servers to in-process SSE/stdio transmission, and directly connected last_assistant_message/last_intent parameters to the dual intent verifier boundary.
Key Insight: The native CLI session API lacks cross-vendor standardization; context-aware routing must explicitly bind historical parameters at the classification boundary rather than relying on implicit or memory state management.
General Issues 5. Wayland/X11 compatibility defects, AionUI syntax/context hallucinations, and SCP path nesting issues disrupted desktop tracking, tool configuration, and cluster upload. Solution: Shifted to D-Bus introspection alternatives for modern operating system environments, verified configuration files against official documentation to correct GUI wrapper assumptions, simplified remote directory structures, and replaced synchronous waiting with asynchronous health check polling.
Key Insight: Traditional window enumeration tools are outdated on modern Linux; GUI wrappers usually lag behind CLI specifications and require direct document verification. Parallel cluster operations require sequential phases or dedicated GPU binding to prevent context leakage and I/O timeout.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Architecture Strategy and Paradigm Shift Role Approach Human Identify core architectural redundancies in traditional manual routing/prompt management, clarify cost/risk priorities, and require proxies to follow cross-platform unified instruction standards. AI Initially adopted gradual hybrid fixes or overly designed custom context loaders, but quickly adapted to a proxy-centric paradigm by implementing lightweight adapters, unified alternative chains, and template-driven prompt generators. Difference Analysis: Humans provide strategic constraints and operational friction insights; AI transform these into tactical infrastructure, handling adversarial threat modeling, cross-platform instruction mapping, and process state bridging without trial and error.
Methodological Verification and Experimental Rigor Role Approach Human Implement multi-stage empirical verification boundaries, explicitly correct misleading metadata-to-execution assumptions, and limit experimental scope to prevent metric confusion. AI Builds automated infrastructure, performs parallel task orchestration, provides systematic diagnostic scripts, but requires clear parameter binding to align with research intent and avoid simulation state confusion. Difference Analysis: Humans apply targeted domain knowledge to define verification thresholds and prevent scope expansion; AI autonomously navigates the code library topology, integrates low-level simulator APIs, while relying on human boundaries for accurate metric calculation.
AI Limitations Key Limitations Overstated reference impact metrics without fully understanding cross-database context, assuming standard CLI context inheritance, generating GUI wrapper commands, and overly confident assertions about data availability based on local metadata states. General Limitations Difficulties in external API authentication boundaries, asynchronous signature detection, and MCP transmission state verification require manual session failure, explicit type checking, and direct interpreter path switching to advance process stages. Unable to autonomously correct absolute paths across environments and parallel orchestration time constraints, forcing the generation of manual scripts, sequential execution alternatives, and asynchronous polling instead of real-time cluster monitoring. Lessons Learned Key Experiences NeurIPS D&B places more emphasis on infrastructure contributions and benchmark meta-evaluation than SOTA declarations; robust construction requires strict cross-environment variable control, multi-dimensional credibility metrics beyond accuracy, and separate evaluation scoring pipelines. Multi-CLI orchestration requires strict alternative abstraction layers; do not rely on native sessions to persist between providers. Context-aware intent routing must explicitly bind historical parameters at the boundary, as scorers cannot reconstruct time dependencies from isolated markers. Data augmentation pipelines must implement closed-loop release verification thresholds, as manifest tags cannot fully guarantee the success of physics-based policies. The wrapping environment should use pattern/metadata stubs rather than full loads to optimize distribution efficiency. MCP server visibility requires a dual-layer mechanism: explicit transmission binding (stdio/SSE) and external discovery configuration. Modern desktop tracking needs D-Bus introspection instead of traditional X11, and asynchronous task loops outperform cron schedulers in high-frequency sampling. CLI proxies must explicitly generate instruction files or dynamically inject at runtime; context propagation cannot rely on memory states or implicit assumptions. GUI wrappers and IDE default settings usually lag behind underlying tool specifications and require direct document verification. Solution: Traced trans_IR scaling factors and dataset loader output, found that metrics are calculated on standardized tensors rather than raw physical units, indicating a process matching error.
Key Insight: Consistent academic benchmark testing requires strict use of raw physical units; incorrect scaler application or inverse transformation is the main cause of differences.
General Issues 3. Multi-process worker crashed due to EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED errors during LIBERO data conversion cleanup, causing preprocessing process interruption. Solution: Registered a clear atexit hook, manually closed the EGL environment and released the GPU context before the Python garbage collector triggers thread termination.
Key Insight: The lifecycle of simulation engine context does not match operating system process termination; resource cleanup must be explicitly managed and cannot rely on default cleanup mechanisms.
4. MIHD project documentation lacks narrative mapping, with active drafts and outdated diagnostic files mixed together, potentially leading to architecture drift. Solution: Performed systematic directory archiving, established a dedicated chart asset repository, and generated a limited dual-language skeleton directly corresponding to visualization goals. Key Insight: Early language separation and direct chart-to-narrative mapping mechanisms can prevent document fragmentation and ensure tight connection between manuscript framework and empirical results.

Implementation Level Battery Dataset Evaluation Expansion and Unit Alignment Role Approach Human Identified existing trans_IR implementations, questioned unnecessary reverse flags, and focused debugging on physical unit alignment and scale application in the battery domain. AI Traced rsm normalization workflow and dataset loader under limited parameters, identified mismatch between normalization domains as the root cause of differences from published baseline metrics. rclone + sync.py completed Google Drive sync for four data categories Investigated GPU partition resources (scavenger-h200 H200×8 available) Installed cchelper skill Key Achievements This Month Identified root cause of MIHD cross-slice retrieval failure and found a solution (2026-03-23, MIHD) — Confirmed root cause is that PCA/STAIG processes each slice independently, producing incomparable embedding spaces. scGPT, due to its shared coordinate system, is the optimal encoder for cross-slice retrieval (average SL@50=0.416, 100% hit rate), revealing the architectural principle that single-slice clustering and cross-slice retrieval require different encoders. Discovered and fixed 4 critical bugs in extract_teddy() (2026-03-29, MIHD) — Systematic source code review revealed: incorrect Tokenizer class name, wrong model forward parameter name (input_ids→gene_ids), wrong output key (last_hidden_state→outputs[‘cell_emb’]), and missing gene symbol to Ensembl ID mapping. After fixes, the first slice (151508, 4384 spots) was successfully validated. Verified STAIG framework’s high robustness to gene encoders (2026-03-30, MIHD) — Teddy 1024d (ARI=0.495) and PCA 50d (ARI=0.497) performed nearly identically under the STAIG framework, with a gap of only 0.002, demonstrating that STAIG’s spatial graph contrastive learning mechanism dominates clustering performance and the impact of gene embedding quality is greatly diluted. Paper Fig 1–6 framework planning completed (2026-03-31, MIHD) — Referencing four competing papers — MISO (Nat Methods), STAIG (Nat Comms), QueST, and Yuan (Nat Methods) — established a complete paper structure: Fig1=framework diagram, Fig2=DLPFC benchmark, Fig3=ablation, Fig4=HD application, Fig5=cross-slice Query, Fig6=Query biological discovery. Written into ECL YAML and plans.md, marking the project’s official transition to the writing phase. TEDDY-G 400M full 11-slice embedding extraction completed (2026-03-30, MIHD) — Completed 1024d gene embedding extraction for all 11 DLPFC slices (151508–151676) in a dedicated conda teddy environment, totaling 185MB, providing a complete data foundation for multi-encoder comparison benchmarks. STHD Ground Truth integration (100% match rate) (2026-03-31, MIHD) — Added _load_sthd_annotations() function, achieving 17502/17502 spots 100% match via r_big/c_big coordinates; CE+Tumor biological merging (Neoplasm + Non-neoplastic Epithelium → Epithelium) yielded 3 meaningful clusters, providing quantitative Ground Truth for HD evaluation. HD full fusion strategy evaluation revealed naive fusion information dilution (2026-03-31, MIHD) — Completed 10/13 HD fusion strategy experiments; found that simple fusion strategies (concat/mean/element_wise_sum) produced ARI (0.19–0.20) lower than unimodal PCA (0.351), while attention fusion approached PCA (ARI=0.342). UNI2 vision-only achieved the highest NMI (0.387) but lower ARI than PCA, revealing that NMI and ARI can be inconsistent across different datasets. Summarized systematic transfer loss pattern of Foundation Models on clustering (2026-03-30, MIHD) — Teddy gene-only ARI (0.186) underperformed PCA (0.255). Systematic analysis confirmed the root cause: Foundation Models are optimized for disease discriminability (not variance maximization), high-dimensional spaces (1024d) degrade KMeans performance, and training data (dissociated scRNA-seq) differs in distribution from spatial transcriptomics. Leiden clustering binary search integration (+15% ARI) (2026-03-31, MIHD) — Implemented binary search in clustering.py to match target n_clusters (range [0.01, 10], up to 20 iterations), enabling fair comparison between Leiden and KMeans. Leiden improved ARI by ~15% over KMeans on DLPFC, but improvement over STAIG was limited. First structured documentation of MIHD project historical issues (2026-03-23, MIHD) — By consolidating plans.md, RESULTS.md, and diagnostic reports, generated docs/PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md — the first centralized record of best ARI 0.546, root cause of cross-slice retrieval failures, fixed bug inventory, and a 4-phase ablation experiment plan, providing a structured entry point for subsequent research. Recurring Issues 1. Systematic failure on a specific slice (151676) (occurred 3 times) Dates: 2026-03-23, 2026-03-30, 2026-03-31 Root Cause: Slice 151676 has data-specific issues: zero-variance embeddings cause mclust to fail and fall back to KMeans (dragging down the global mean), and model collapse under the STAIG framework cannot be recovered. The root cause remains unidentified, possibly related to anomalous gene expression distribution or spatial structure in this slice. Status: 🔄 Ongoing
2. Pipeline hardcoded configuration inconsistent with slice-specific parameters (occurred 2 times) Dates: 2026-03-30, 2026-03-31 Root Cause: Pipeline global configuration (e.g., top_genes=3000, dataset defaults, image path structure) has implicit divergences from slice-specific config (151676 uses 5000 genes) or dataset-specific structure (HD vs DLPFC image paths), causing cache check false positives (sys.exit) and visual extraction failures. Status: 🔧 Workaround available
3. HPC environment configuration obstacles (conda activation, missing config files) (occurred 2 times) Dates: 2026-03-23, 2026-03-31 Root Cause: Config files do not automatically migrate to new machines (sync.json must be manually reconstructed), and conda initialization on SLURM compute nodes differs from login nodes (requires eval $(conda shell.bash hook) rather than source activate). Both issues stem from a lack of experience with environment migration. Status: ✅ Resolved
4. Cross-session context loss requiring repeated background provision (occurred 2 times) Dates: 2026-03-23, 2026-03-29 Root Cause: Claude’s session isolation mechanism means key research progress (e.g., Teddy test results) is not persisted to the memory system, requiring users to re-provide arXiv links or background information in subsequent sessions. Status: 🔄 Ongoing
Human-AI Collaboration Trends Human-led key insights: 7 AI limitation pattern: Cross-session memory loss: context at critical research milestones is not automatically persisted, requiring users to repeatedly provide background AI limitation pattern: Hardcoded assumptions delay bug discovery: defaults to global config rather than dynamically resolving slice-specific parameters, tracing root causes only after actual errors occur AI limitation pattern: Excessive reliance on cluster resources: unable to proactively judge whether small datasets (17502 spots) require GPU/SLURM, defaulting to job submission AI limitation pattern: Convention assumptions about non-standard APIs: assumed HuggingFace standard interfaces without reading source code, leading to 4 TEDDY API usage errors AI limitation pattern: Inefficient monitoring strategy: background tasks used multi-round sleep+ls polling instead of event-driven mechanisms Improvement direction: Proactively trigger memory persistence at critical research milestones to avoid cross-session context loss Improvement direction: Proactively identify path/parameter dataset-specific risks when dealing with multi-dataset pipelines Improvement direction: Do not assume API conventions for non-standard libraries before reading source code; declare upfront that verification is needed Improvement direction: Provide proactive experiment prioritization suggestions rather than just listing options and waiting for user decisions Improvement direction: Estimate compute requirements based on data scale, distinguishing locally runnable tasks from those requiring the cluster Selected Insights This Month Architecture STAIG framework is highly robust to gene encoders: Teddy 1024d vs PCA 50d under STAIG shows only 0.002 ARI difference, demonstrating that spatial graph contrastive learning dominates clustering performance and the impact of gene embedding quality is greatly diluted. Therefore, the bottleneck for optimizing MIHD clustering performance does not lie in the choice of gene encoder. (Source: 2026-03-30) The optimal encoder for single-slice clustering (STAIG/PCA) differs from the optimal encoder for cross-slice retrieval (scGPT): the comparability of embedding spaces (shared coordinate system) is more critical than local quality. Foundation Models naturally suit cross-slice retrieval due to their fixed representation space output, while PCA processes slices independently, producing incomparable coordinate systems. (Source: 2026-03-23) Foundation Models exhibit systematic transfer loss on cross-domain downstream tasks: TEDDY achieves SOTA on disease classification (ACC=0.72) but underperforms PCA on spatial transcriptomics clustering (ARI 0.186 vs 0.255). Root cause is optimization objective mismatch (discriminative representation vs variance maximization), and high-dimensional space (1024d) is unfavorable for KMeans. (Source: 2026-03-30) Domain Knowledge HVG1500 (direct concatenation of highly variable genes without dimensionality reduction) achieves ARI=0.330 on single slices, outperforming all Foundation Models; Leiden clustering improves ARI by ~15% over KMeans on DLPFC, but improvement over STAIG is limited — STAIG’s advantage comes from spatial graph structure and is relatively independent of the clustering algorithm. (Source: 2026-03-30, 2026-03-31) NMI and ARI show inconsistency on HD data: UNI2 vision-only achieves the highest NMI (0.387) but lower ARI than PCA (0.344 vs 0.351); naive fusion (concat/mean) on HD yields ARI (0.19–0.20) lower than unimodal PCA (0.351), indicating information dilution from simple fusion. Both metrics should be reported together. (Source: 2026-03-31) Tools Single-cell foundation model forward interfaces in the HuggingFace ecosystem vary significantly and standard interfaces cannot be assumed: TEDDY uses gene_ids (not input_ids), GeneTokenizer (not Tokenizer), outputs[‘cell_emb’] (not last_hidden_state), and its vocab uses Ensembl IDs (43808 tokens) rather than gene symbols. Source code must be read to confirm. (Source: 2026-03-29) DCC HPC cluster practical notes: SLURM compute nodes require eval $(conda shell.bash hook) && conda activate to initialize conda (source activate does not work); scavenger-h200 provides H200×8 preemptible nodes; account TRES limits are cpu=100/mem=500G; Glob tends to time out on large HPC filesystems — use exact path search instead. (Source: 2026-03-23, 2026-03-31) Debugging Implicit divergence between slice-specific configuration (e.g., staig num_gene) and pipeline global defaults is a high-risk bug type: cache check logic should dynamically resolve actual configuration rather than hardcoding defaults; multi-dataset pipeline image paths should be explicitly differentiated rather than using a unified data_root/section_id logic. TokenMonitor’s Claude parser caused cost duplication through mirrored JSONL files, while the GitHub Actions workflow stagnated due to step-level confidential assessment limitations and macOS signature fallback failures. Solution: Isolate message attributes to achieve semantic deduplication (best practice), elevate dynamic credentials to job-level environment variables, correct the build chain, and implement supplier rate table filtering to ensure billing accuracy.

Weekly Report — 2026-W13 (2026-03-23 ~ 2026-03-29) This week’s core work focused on multi-model embedding expansion and issue triage for the MIHD spatial transcriptomics project. On March 23, environment initialization was completed on the DCC HPC cluster, and historical challenges in the MIHD project were systematically documented — for the first time structuring the root cause of cross-section retrieval failure (incomparable embedding spaces) and the single-section ARI gap as formal documents. On March 29, four critical bugs in the TEDDY foundation model extraction script were successfully fixed, the first DLPFC section embedding extraction was completed, and batch runs were launched, establishing the foundation for a multi-model comparison benchmark.

Systematically reviewed historical issues and persisted them as docs/PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md, including root cause analysis of cross-section retrieval failure Identified root cause of cross-section task failure: PCA/STAIG independent processing produces incomparable embedding coordinate systems; scGPT shared space achieves average SL@50=0.416 Fixed 4 critical bugs in the extract_teddy() script, successfully completed TEDDY embedding extraction for section 151508 (4384 spots) Launched batch TEDDY embedding extraction for the remaining 10 DLPFC sections, establishing a four-model comparison framework: scGPT/Geneformer/C2S/TEDDY Blockers:
⚠️ Single-section ARI remains below target (current 0.546 vs. target 0.60+); 4-phase ablation experiment plan not yet executed ⚠️ Root cause of mclust falling back to KMeans due to zero-variance embedding in section 151676 unknown ⚠️ Batch TEDDY embedding extraction (10 sections) still running as of March 29 DCC HPC Cluster Environment Initialization (1 active day) — ✅ completed Completed:
Configured rclone sync.json; completed sync of 4 data categories (summarize/research/test/website) via sync.py pull Investigated GPU resources: common (RTX 2080), scavenger-gpu (A6000/RTX 5000-6000 Ada), scavenger-h200 (H200×8) Installed cchelper skill to ~/.claude/skills/cchelper/ Key Tasks ✅ Fixed 4 critical bugs in extract_teddy() script (2026-03-29) — Discovered and fixed via systematic source code review: ① incorrect import of Tokenizer changed to GeneTokenizer; ② model forward parameter input_ids changed to gene_ids; ③ output access last_hidden_state changed to outputs[‘cell_emb’]; ④ added gene symbol to Ensembl ID mapping logic. ✅ MIHD project issue review and documentation (2026-03-23) — Reviewed current state of the MIHD project (best ARI 0.546, root cause of cross-section retrieval failure, list of fixed bugs), generated structured issue summary document docs/PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md. ✅ TEDDY paper analysis and architecture evaluation (2026-03-29) — Analyzed arXiv 2503.03485, reviewed TEDDY model architecture (Teddy-G/X two encoding types, 6 variants, up to 400M parameters), evaluated performance on disease classification benchmarks (held-out donor multi-class classification 8% higher than Nicheformer, linear probe far superior to fine-tuning). 🔄 DLPFC embedding batch extraction (2026-03-29) — Extracting 1024-dimensional cell embeddings for 11 DLPFC sections in the teddy conda environment; section 151508 complete, remaining 10 sections still running. Issues and Solutions 1. TEDDY extraction script used a non-existent Tokenizer class and incorrect model API (input_ids, last_hidden_state), making the script completely non-functional [MIHD] (2026-03-29) Solution: Read TEDDY source code to confirm correct API: GeneTokenizer, gene_ids parameter, outputs[‘cell_emb’] output key, and added Ensembl ID mapping (60% of genes in the DLPFC dataset are mappable)
2. MIHD cross-section retrieval almost completely failed (10 out of 14 query directions with SL@50=0) [MIHD] (2026-03-23) Solution: Diagnosed root cause as PCA/STAIG independent processing per section producing incomparable embedding spaces; switched to scGPT embeddings (shared space), achieving average SL@50=0.416 with 100% hit rate
3. TEDDY inference with batch_size=32 caused GPU OOM (32GB VRAM), because each sequence is up to 2048 tokens long [MIHD] (2026-03-29) Solution: Reduced batch_size from 32 to 8, bringing memory usage under control
4. New DCC machine had no ~/.config/gadget/sync.json, preventing sync.py from running [DCC Environment Initialization] (2026-03-23) Solution: Inferred rclone_remote configuration from existing summarize config, manually created sync.json and verified remote directory structure before executing pull
Learnings Domain Knowledge (domain) In cross-section tasks in spatial transcriptomics, the comparability of embedding spaces (shared coordinate system) is more critical than local embedding quality. Foundation models (scGPT/TEDDY) are naturally suited for cross-section retrieval due to their fixed representation spaces; PCA/STAIG independent processing produces incomparable coordinate systems and is not suitable for cross-section tasks. The optimal method for single-section clustering (STAIG) and the optimal method for cross-section retrieval (scGPT) are different; different encoders should be selected for different task objectives, and a unified optimal solution should not be pursued. TEDDY-G (rank-value encoding) outperforms TEDDY-X (binned expression); linear probe far outperforms fine-tuning (RA: 0.56→0.93), indicating high embedding quality but susceptibility to overfitting during fine-tuning; 8% higher than Nicheformer on held-out donor multi-class classification. Tools (tools) Single-cell foundation models in the HuggingFace ecosystem (TEDDY, scGPT, etc.) have significantly different forward interfaces; standard HuggingFace interfaces cannot be assumed. Source code must be read to confirm the gene_ids parameter name and output dict structure. TEDDY’s vocab uses Ensembl IDs (43808 tokens) rather than gene symbols. Architecture (architecture) TEDDY uses rank-value encoding, retaining the top 2048 genes as a token sequence. The sequence length is longer than models like scGPT, resulting in higher VRAM requirements and the need for smaller batch sizes during inference. AI Usage Notes Effective patterns:
✓ Systematic code review (read source → verify API → compare implementation), proactively discovering hidden bugs unknown to the user, saving debugging time ✓ Choosing to confirm rather than guess when requirements are ambiguous (private file sync requirements), avoiding incorrect execution ✓ Persisting verbal analysis results as structured documents (PROBLEM_SUMMARY.md), completing knowledge externalization with user initiative Limitations:
✗ Cross-session memory not persisted: unable to recall previous TEDDY test discussions, requiring users to re-provide background information ✗ PDF parsing failure: unable to process binary content when directly fetching arXiv PDFs, requiring fallback to HTML version ✗ Relies on existing documentation for project summaries; cannot infer undocumented implicit progress or autonomously prioritize ablation experiments Outlook for Next Week Next week’s priorities: ① Confirm completion of batch TEDDY embedding extraction (10 DLPFC sections) and integrate four-model (scGPT/Geneformer/C2S/TEDDY) comparative evaluation results; ② Execute the 4-phase ablation experiments in the MIHD single-section ARI improvement plan, focusing on diagnosing the root cause of zero-variance embeddings in section 151676; ③ Based on multi-model comparison results, decide whether a combined encoder strategy is needed (scGPT for cross-section, STAIG for single-section clustering).

Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ Designed and implemented cchypothesis skill — Designed and coded a hypothesis-based debugging workflow skill, including SKILL.md, slash command configuration, diagnostic mode, and ECL planning documentation. ✅ Resolved Footer/app layout offset issues during scaling — Separated the footer from the flex container, applied position: fixed for viewport alignment, and called native IPC after synchronizing #app height via JS to eliminate continuous visual jitter. ✅ Unified BOSS evaluation script logs — Modified eval_boss44.py, eval_oss_ch.py, and eval_skill_chain.py to always record the success rate and average metrics of each task, saving them in JSON format regardless of the save_stats flag. ✅ Implemented cross-platform window bottom edge anchoring — Updated the Rust window positioning logic for Windows/macOS/Linux to correctly detect top/bottom alignment and maintain anchoring edges during scaling operations. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Fixed TokenMonitor chart hover flicker issue — Reduced fadeout time, removed DOM keyframe switch wrapper, simplified hide process, and added effect protection mechanisms to resolve visual issues in the detail panel. ✅ Resolved upward movement of window bottom edge after height change — Changed anchor detection from a fixed threshold to direct gap comparison top_gap <= bottom_gap, used current rectangle boundaries instead of working area limits to correct the bottom anchor Y value calculation, and updated cross-platform limit logic. ✅ Fixed critical UI/animation synchronization issues in TokenMonitor Tauri app — Resolved UI/animation synchronization issues through architectural layout adjustments. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Due to a 1-frame delay between SetWindowPos IPC calls and CSS repaint cycles, the footer and application bottom edge move continuously during window scaling. Solution: Move the footer out of the dynamic flex container and apply position: fixed; bottom: 0 to bypass the layout queue. Pre-set #app min-height via JS, then achieve DOM and native synchronization before sending IPC commands, thereby filling the delay gap.
Key Insight: The cross-stack frame delay between native C API window management and WebView2/CSS cannot be fully compensated by Flexbox or CSS transitions; absolute viewport anchoring and pre-layout synchronization are essential for pixel-level stability.
2. The window bottom edge jumps upward after height change, sometimes falling below the taskbar area in Windows systems. Solution: Change anchor detection from a fixed threshold to direct gap comparison top_gap <= bottom_gap, use current rectangle boundaries instead of working area limits to correct the bottom anchor Y value calculation, and update cross-platform limit logic.
Key Insight: Edge anchoring must dynamically track the nearest physical boundary rather than relying on static pixel thresholds; limits should retain the initial position and only intervene when crossing a safe area.
General Issues 3. Chart hover detail panel flickers and jumps during bar changes, caused by DOM destruction/reconstruction and timer race conditions. Solution: Shorten fadeout time to 150ms, remove {#key} trigger block to keep DOM elements intact, merge two-stage hide process, and add boundary protection mechanisms for layout measurement effects.
Key Insight: Svelte’s key blocks force complete component destruction; maintaining DOM nodes alive while updating reactive properties avoids visual duplicates during rapid state changes.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Debugging Skill Architecture Role Method Human Defined a structured scientific debugging process: classification → generate verifiable hypotheses → parallel read-only investigation → serial repair/verification → iterative reporting. AI AI follows human architectural constraints, expands them into phased requirements, conducts adversarial review, identifies edge cases (context budget, file conflicts), and generates a complete implementation framework. Analysis of Differences: Humans provide core methods and control flow; AI achieves architectural rigor, formalizes verification rules, and handles cross-file dependency mapping.
UI/UX Layout Stability Diagnosis Role Method Human Identified specific visual metrics (moving “X years ago” footer text) as decisive indicators of layout instability, and recommended using position: fixed as a basic repair solution. AI Initially tried CSS Flexbox compensation and animation curve coordination. Under human guidance, AI shifted to DOM extraction, absolute positioning, and synchronizing pre-layout height before IPC transmission. Analysis of Differences: Humans correctly identified that CSS-level layout calculations cannot resolve native rendering race conditions and guided the architecture toward viewport anchoring; AI successfully achieved this transition.
AI Limitations Key Limitations AI initially struggled to solve cross-stack frame delay issues using only CSS/Flexbox, requiring multiple iterations to realize the need for absolute positioning and JS pre-layout. General Limitations AI has other limitations. - AI cannot parse binary video files uploaded by humans for visual symptom analysis, so it defaults to code-based root-cause tracking. Learning Insights Key Learning Points When native window management APIs (such as Win32 SetWindowPos) and web rendering operate asynchronously, absolute viewport anchoring or pre-measuring and applying sizes on the JavaScript side before IPC calls are required to ensure visual stability. Using position: fixed can completely bypass CSS layout repaint queues related to parent container animations, making it the most reliable method for stabilizing UI elements during dynamic host size changes. Practical Learning Points A hypothesis-driven debugging workflow significantly reduces confirmation bias by forcing parallel investigation and mandatory evidence recording. Per-section PCA/STAIG produce non-comparable embedding spaces, 10 out of 14 combinations in cross-slice retrieval have SL@50=0, normalize cannot fix [MIHD spatial transcriptome] (2026-03-16) Solution: Use pre-trained Foundation Model (scGPT): all slices share the same model weights, output is naturally in the same coordinate system; SL@50 increased from 0.013 to 0.416, hit rate 100%. Root cause is inconsistent coordinate systems (mathematically impossible to normalize), not insufficient gene feature information
2. CompositeBodyObject breaks during env.reset() (lid floating, base offset), but normal during HDF5 playback (set_sim_state_flat covering body position hides the problem) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-16) Solution: Add locations_relative_to_corner instance attribute in generated_objects.py__init__, restore coordinate transformation logic from corner to center (aligned in commit 398af01b); all 139 unit tests pass
3. After the vla_infer.py task completes but current_prompt is not cleared, if chunk_count in the next loop is still ≥5 and the model score remains high, the done message is triggered again immediately, leading to an infinite loop reporting completion [robobrain_pi] (2026-03-17) Solution: Add current_prompt=’’ and publise_state(‘idle’) at the end of the task completion block; the state machine must reset both the trigger condition and the broadcast state change simultaneously upon completion
5. π₀.₅ Pi0WithCompletionHead uses a combination approach that adds pi0/ prefix to all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to throw ‘2 children vs 1 child’ ValueError, and checkpoints cannot be loaded at all [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Change to inheritance (class Pi0WithCompletionHead(Pi0)), and align Pi0 parameters directly with the checkpoint path at the top level; inheritance in Flax NNX is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility

RobotwinOutputs.call only returns the {actions} field, silently discarding manip_progress; even if the model correctly predicts the progress field, external parties can never obtain it, and the eval txt file remains empty always [π₀.₅] (2026-03-18) Solution: Modify the return dict of the output transform to include the manip_progress field, and re-establish the data flow; to troubleshoot such bugs, track upward from the end of the data flow

In MIHD all_aligned mode, the –alignment parameter is not injected during the evaluate phase, so EvaluationJob.alignment remains None, Harmony alignment results are completely ignored, and the alignment function actually fails [MIHD spatial transcriptomics] (2026-03-18) Solution: Add 3 lines of code before the run_pipeline.py evaluate phase: when phase==‘all_aligned’ and args.alignment has a value, inject alignment into extra_config for each experiment
9. drop_in_transit_D0 generates very few valid scenarios, with min_hold_height=0.85 being too low; objects on the desktop (z≈0.88) are misclassified as in the air, resulting in 80% false positives [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-20) Solution: Raise the threshold to 0.93 (desktop height 0.80 + Milk object height 0.08 + margin 0.05), eliminating false positives, and increasing D0 success rate from 10% to 50%
10. python summarize/daily_summary.py gets stuck permanently at @ccusage/codex step, with no output or error [gadget] (2026-03-21) Solution: Use subprocess.run(capture_output=True) to redirect stdin to DEVNULL, and the npx installation prompt for the first time forces infinite waiting; add –yes parameter to skip interactive confirmation in all 3 npx calls
11. In multi-object tasks like threading/pick_place, phase detection fails systematically, and all frames in threading are marked as pre_reach, causing 12/13 skills to fail to find an opportunity [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-21) Solution: Add InteractionSegmenter to segment trajectories by object interactions (EEF proximity + gripper state + co-motion detection), clearly define target_object and phase for each segment; completely bypass single-object phase detection instead of fixing the defect—increase threading subtypes from 3 to 25
12. The Panda robotic arm gripper action polarity is opposite to the code assumption: Panda requires action=+1 to close, but hardcoding -1 actually opens the gripper, leading to all injections for coffee/stack failing [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Detect polarity via robot arm type in EnvWrapper.init, set PandaGripper to close_action=+1.0, and RethinkGripper to -1.0; add a helper and replace all hardcoded actions [-1]
13. drop_with_interaction generates 0 scenes for all tasks: the original implementation only applies a 1–3 cm offset before releasing, and objects spaced 10–20 cm never touch neighbors [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-22) Solution: Rewrite the inject logic: actively move the object directly above the non-target (+0.15m), then release the gripper to allow free fall, and track object-object contact throughout the settle process
Learning Insights Architecture Pipeline contract alignment must track the complete data flow: not only modify processing logic but also ensure data is persisted at the storage layer (e.g., segment_interactions() results written to NPZ); output transform is an implicit filter in the inference chain, and any field not in the return dict is silently discarded; CLI parameters in multi-stage pipelines must be explicitly passed to each downstream stage, not relying on implicit sharing. “Passing unit tests ≠ E2E correctness” In multi-object robot manipulation tasks, target_object must pass through all three stages (detector/injector/validator) as a primary citizen; objects[0] is the first object in dictionary insertion order, and using it in multi-object scenarios causes complete semantic errors without errors, leading to systematic misjudgments based on object state. graspable objects and fixtures must be distinguished by the grasp_geoms field, and target selection cannot rely solely on distance/position Independent processing per section (PCA/training) produces non-comparable embedding spaces, which is a fundamental architectural limitation and cannot be fixed through normalization or post-processing. The only correct zero-shot solution is pre-trained Foundation Model (shared weights). Gene FM (scGPT 100%) outperforms Vision FM (UNI2 71%) because gene expression has stronger cross-sample consistency due to the batch effect in H&E images Flax NNX extended models: inheritance (class Child(Parent)) is the only way to keep checkpoint path compatibility; combination (self.pi0 = Pi0(…)) adds a prefix before all parent module parameter paths, causing pytree merge to fail completely. The freezing mechanism (freeze_filter+nnx.DiffState) in existing frameworks usually considers scalability—prioritize reuse over creation Facing architectural design flaws, “bypassing” is more fundamental than “fixing”: the single-object phase detection assumption cannot be fixed through parameter tuning; directly bypassing it with InteractionSegmenter is a more elegant solution. Do not fix but bypass the flawed abstraction level Debugging State machine design principle: completing an event must do two things simultaneously—reset trigger conditions (clear current_prompt) and broadcast state change (_publish_state(‘idle’)). Doing only one of them leaves hidden bugs like infinite loops or upstream perception failure. None checks must precede any property access (defensive programming) When diagnosing behavior of unknown third-party libraries, writing a minimal test script is more reliable and efficient than static code analysis (robosuite gripper polarity case); log counter statistics are more effective for locating systematic bugs than reading each entry (1698 occurrences of ‘gripper not closed’ directly point to target_object ambiguity); troubleshoot implicit filtering bugs by tracking upward from the data flow Experiment naming conventions must strictly match actual implementation; inconsistent naming like “pca_uni2_staig_fusion” leads to long-term misunderstandings, and actual configuration must be confirmed by reading logs rather than just experiment names. Benchmark data quality issues (uneven distribution, all phase annotations as pre_reach) should include monitoring mechanisms during pipeline design Tools subprocess.run(capture_output=True) redirects stdin to DEVNULL, and CLI tools with interactive prompts (npx, etc.) must use –yes/-y, otherwise they hang indefinitely instead of timing out. capture_output=True is the high-level cause of hanging Slurm HPC cluster’s pam_slurm_adopt policy kills all related processes at job end, and SSH nohup cannot bypass this; long training tasks must submit formal jobs with sbatch. MuJoCo physics simulation (enable_camera=False) is a pure CPU task, and MUJOCO_GL=disabled can completely bypass OpenGL, with worker count exactly matching –cpus-per-task JAX has_aux mechanism: nnx.value_and_grad supports has_aux=True, compute_loss returns (loss_array, aux_dict) after which gradients are calculated only for loss_array, and aux_dict transparently carries monitoring metrics; stop_gradient strictly limits aux loss to MLP parameters, and the numerical ratio of action/aux loss does not indicate training imbalance Hugo best practices: .Title is the most stable field for identifying specific sections (.Section and.RelPermalink case sensitivity varies across platforms); static directory names matching content page base names cause path conflicts; auto-generated frontmatter should not use current system time as date; project-level layouts/partials can cover themes partially without forking the theme Spatial data nearest-neighbor query: Large point clouds (>10K points) should prioritize KD tree (O(N log N) preprocessing) instead of cdist (O(N²) memory); in HD spatial transcriptomics (17K+ cells), differences can reach OOM vs normal operation. Single truth source principle: constants referenced across multiple files must be imported from the only defined place Domain Knowledge- Recovery Behavior Group (RBG) grouping strategy: 29 error subtypes are clustered into 5 groups based on motor primitives, and demos within the same group can be cross‑augmented. MimicGen generates over 1,000 demos from 10 source demos; 1,740 simple requirements are compressed to 329 (saving 81%). This is a paradigm applicable widely to robot recovery data engineering. π₀.₅ computational graph characteristics: Reasoning follows a natural two‑step process (VLM prefix forward → action expert denoising). During training, Exp1–4 can be combined into one joint forward using teacher forcing. The from_hidden mode introduces circular dependencies due to the dependence on model output for conditioning, requiring an additional prefix‑only forward. Mean pooling of prefix_output is more suitable for classification tasks than suffix_output of action expert (for encoding global state understanding). The depth of LLM understanding in academic trajectory analysis exceeds expectations: It can automatically identify advanced features such as ‘infrastructure‑thinking researchers’ and ‘technical prerequisites for paradigm shifts’. The why_not_before field (attributing each breakthrough to data, compute, and insight across three dimensions) is the most valuable feature in researcher profiling. The recognition of conference awards has very low ROI with current LLM capabilities; it should be replaced by an external data source solution (exact title matching JSON library). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:

Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. VLA training loss becomes stable, but task completion accuracy stagnates due to extremely high class imbalance (approximately 4% positive samples), leading to gradient suppression and misleading convergence metrics. Solution: Mathematically proven that the negative sample dominance phenomenon occurs, applied pos_weight=10 in Sigmoid BCE loss, and refactored inference loop by sharing VLM prefix features via KV cache, achieving unified processing, thereby restoring balanced gradient signals and eliminating redundant computation. Key Insight: Stable total loss does not guarantee performance for minority classes; when imbalance exceeds 90/10, direct sample weighting is more effective than complex sampling, and the side-class discriminator must be stacked multiple times into initial feature extraction to avoid rapid latency increase.
2. Calendar routing treats multi-day queries as general fallback or No events, due to lack of intent description in BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, hard-coded keyword thresholds, and failed timestamp parsing causing excessive automatic scheduler duplication. Solution: Insert a clear query intent classification table into the base prompt, add robust keyword fallback detection in the processor, correct ISO parsing logic to prioritize start time over display string, enable include_past=True, and removed 53 duplicate entries via target CLI cleanup.
Key Insight: Dictionary-defined intent segments are ignored unless explicitly merged during runtime; strict double-layer verification would break secondary command intentions, while direct multi-intent decomposition provides clearer routing without losing accuracy.
3. Daily log export pipeline and cross-device synchronization workflow are silently skipped or stalled due to traditional _finalized default value (True) in merge logic, leading to infinite processing loops and wasted computational resources in distributed rclone. Solution: Set state flag fallback to conservative False value in CLI parser, add clear --force reconstruction path, change historical merge from strict boolean dependency to time expiration (>1 day), ensuring pipeline replay and synchronization stability.
Key Insight: Batch processing of state flags must use conservative default values; mismatched default values or hard Boolean gates in distributed workflows silently fail and block the entire dataset lock, unless combined with time-override strategy.
4. MimicGen trajectory enhancement bypasses spatial transformation by injecting heuristic noise instead of coordinate differences, causing failure during object pose changes in synthetic recovery demonstrations; hard-coded paths also undermine cross-machine portability. Solution: Modify _replay_with_warping to map exact coordinate differences between source and target before execution, replace absolute PROJECT_ROOT definitions with dynamic __file__ resolution, enabling deployment completely independent of path in isolated settings.
Key Insight: Trajectory transmission requires exact coordinate difference mapping rather than noise injection; true modular benchmark tools must be strictly independent of paths to avoid failure during external deployment due to environment mismatches.
General Issues 5. OS-level vendor daemons on macOS monopolize HID devices, causing obstacles in SpaceMouse remote operations, while zombie GPU processes on tianhe nodes hide VRAM leaks by abandoning monitoring daemons (nvtop/wandb), hindering allocation. Solution: Solve HID conflicts by enumerating original product IDs, terminate competing 3Dconnexion drivers, cover target IDs; identify real PID through /proc/PID/fd processing program, stop nvidia driver to ensure safe termination, thereby clearing virtual GPU locks.

Enes Eken — Research Report Analysis Analysis Mode: fast | Analysis Time: 2026-03-16T00:57:05
Rating: Active Researcher (30.2/100) Basic Metrics Metric Value Institution Unknown h-index 7 Total Citations 138 Citations in Last 5 Years 17 Total Papers 21 Papers Presented at Top Conferences 0 Publication Period 2014 - 2025 Semantic Scholar 2072299 Research Trajectory Enes Eken’s academic career shows a clear three-stage evolution. The first phase (2014–2018) focused on the reliability design of Spin Transfer Torque RAM (STT-RAM), forming a certain technical accumulation around read/write reliability enhancement, variation-aware simulation tools, and error-correcting code schemes. All its highest-cited papers come from this period. The second phase (2021–2022) shifted toward research on Generative Adversary Network (GAN) evaluation methods, focusing on using the Fréchet distance to measure GAN overfitting/underfitting issues, but overall citation response was limited. The third phase (2023–2025) turned to the cross-application of laser spectroscopy technology and deep learning, using Transformer models to process spectral data of quantum cascaded lasers and engaging in target detection, showing a scattered direction.
Overall, this researcher is a contributor who develops steadily within a medium-impact range, rather than a leading figure in the field. With an h-index of 7, 138 total citations, and only 17 citations in the last five years, it indicates that multiple shifts in research directions have led to insufficient continuous deepening of citation accumulation. There are currently no results published at top conferences (such as NeurIPS, ISSCC, DAC A level). The core feature of his academic trajectory is crossing three significantly different fields: hardware architecture, machine learning, and optical sensing, showing application-oriented flexibility, but also sacrificing deep accumulation in a single direction.
Breakthrough Works 1. A Novel Self-Reference Technique for STT-RAM Read and Write Reliability Enhancement (2014) Description: A self-reference reading scheme was proposed, introducing an adaptive reference current comparison mechanism during reading operations, while enhancing the read and write reliability of STT-RAM and reducing the probability of misreading and miswriting.
Why It Could Not Be Achieved Before: Early research on STT-RAM mainly focused on the device physics level, with insufficient systematic modeling of how process variations and thermal fluctuations jointly affect the read/write window; there was previously a lack of a methodological framework that unified self-reference schemes with write reliability enhancement.
Impact: It opened up a direction in STT-RAM reliability circuit design, being cited in multiple simulation tool and ECC scheme papers, laying the foundation for 24 citations in this field.
2. NVSim-VXs: An Improved NVSim for Variation Aware STT-RAM Simulation (2016) Description: Based on the open-source NVSim simulation framework, a process variation modeling module was introduced, enabling researchers to quantitatively evaluate the trade-off between yield and performance of STT-RAM, and output delay, power consumption, and area estimates with variation awareness.
Why It Could Not Be Achieved Before: The original NVSim assumes nominal process parameters and lacks statistical variation modeling capabilities; before the variation effects were significantly amplified at nodes below 7nm, the industry did not have urgent needs for variation-aware simulation tools, and relevant variation parameter databases were not fully published.
Impact: This paper, with 17 citations, became the third-highest cited paper of this researcher, providing a practical tool for exploring the design space of STT-RAM and also promoting subsequent manufacturing cost modeling work (2016 IGSC paper).
3. Sliding Basket: An Adaptive ECC Scheme for Runtime Write Failure Suppression of STT-RAM Cache (2016) Description: A dynamic adaptive error-correcting code scheme was proposed, adjusting the ECC strength and cache line mapping strategy according to the runtime write failure rate, achieving runtime balance between hardware overhead and reliability.
Why It Could Not Be Achieved Before: Traditional static ECC schemes fix the protection strength during design, and cannot adapt to the characteristics of STT-RAM write latency and failure rate that vary dynamically with temperature and aging; sufficient statistical understanding of the runtime features of write failure distributions is required to design an adaptive strategy.
Impact: 16 citations, providing new ideas for runtime-optimized ECC design for STT-RAM cache, and was published at the DATE conference, having certain dissemination effect.
4. Recent Technology Advances of Emerging Memories (2017) Description: A review of the latest progress in emerging memory technologies such as STT-RAM, PCM, and RRAM, systematically outlining the challenges and opportunities of various non-volatile memories at the device physics, circuit design, and system application levels.
Why It Could Not Be Achieved Before: Such review papers benefited from a specific time point—around 2017, when emerging memory technologies entered large-scale production. Both the industry and academia needed a cross-sectional comparison that took into account device, circuit, and system perspectives; previous similar reviews were scattered and not systematic enough.
Impact: 25 citations, the highest-cited single paper of this researcher, indicating that review-type work has high dissemination value in aggregated domain cognition.
5. A novel breath molecule sensing system based on deep neural network employing multiple-line direct absorption spectroscopy (2023) Description: Deep neural networks were applied to multi-line direct absorption spectroscopy data analysis, enabling high-precision detection of various molecules in exhaled breath and providing a technical path for non-invasive medical diagnosis.
Why It Could Not Be Achieved Before: Early spectroscopy analysis relied on traditional numerical fitting algorithms (such as Voigt line fitting), with limited ability to handle noise and overlapping peaks; the engineering problem of deploying large-scale deep learning models in resource-constrained sensor scenarios was not basically solved until the 2020s, and the accumulation of high-quality exhaled breath spectral annotation datasets also required time.
Impact: 12 citations, the highest-cited paper among this researcher’s recent work, indicating that he has certain research capabilities in the cross-field of laser spectroscopy + AI, but this direction is still early, and its influence remains to be evaluated.
Research Directions STT-RAM reliability design and variation-aware simulation (2014–2018) GAN evaluation methods and Fréchet distance application (2021–2022) Cross-application of laser spectroscopy technology and deep learning/Transformer models (2023–2025) Target detection network architecture design (2025) Methodological Evolution Early (2014–2018) methodology centered on hardware architecture design and circuit-level simulation, relying on SPICE simulation, variation statistical modeling, and VHDL/Verilog implementation, emphasizing manufacturability and process robustness; the tool contribution (NVSim-VXs) was a typical output of this phase.
After 2021, methodology shifted to data-driven approaches, first using subspace analysis of weight matrices in GAN training to improve evaluation metrics, then turning to Transformer encoders for handling temporal spectral data. This evolution reflects that the popularity of deep learning toolboxes reduced the threshold for cross-domain migration, but also led to relatively limited depth accumulation of methodology at each stage—from hardware simulation to GAN evaluation to spectral modeling, the three transitions lack intrinsic methodological continuity, and it is more about changing application scenarios rather than continuous evolution of core methods.
Field Impact Enes Eken’s contributions to the field are mainly reflected in two specific aspects: the STT-RAM design toolchain (NVSim-VXs) and reliability methods (self-reference technique, Sliding Basket ECC). During the active period of non-volatile memory research from 2014–2017, he provided valuable practical tools and schemes, with approximately 110 citations from this phase. His impact is limited to the STT-RAM subfield and he has not left a landmark influence in broader computer architecture or electronic design automation fields. Although his research direction shift after 2021 shows interdisciplinary adaptability, citation data (only 17 in the last five years) indicate that he has not established significant influence in new directions. Overall evaluation: This researcher is a qualified contributor to the STT-RAM field, but not a core figure shaping the field’s direction.
