Daily Report — 2026-03-15 General Overview Completed Work: Implemented cross-project development, including unifying research tools, shifting benchmark testing paradigms from physical injection mode to quota-driven semantic mode, aligning VLA pipeline data patterns, and fixing infrastructure environment issues. Implementation Methods: Merged old modules through import tracking isolation, used multi-backend LLM routing to unify CLI pipelines, corrected JAX/PyTorch tensor broadcasting and CUDA ABI dependency issues, deployed the /proc file system inspection function, and performed strict git index cleanup of macOS metadata. Impact: Established a clean and optimized v5 benchmark foundation, improved VLA training efficiency through precise data loaders and model alignment, enhanced research automation security via MCP stdio isolation, and eliminated continuous pipeline crashes caused by old state logic and localization differences. DCC Completed Work: Remained active, but no direct AI interaction logs were recorded during the reporting period. Implementation Methods: None Impact: All active nodes’ daily workload and architectural progress were fully captured, and there was no resource fragmentation issue. MacBook Completed Work: Implemented MCP server tools, resolved the finalization bottleneck in daily summaries, cleaned macOS hidden files from git indexes, and tracked VLA training loss fluctuations. Implementation Methods: Used a context manager with strict stdout isolation to call the FastMCP framework, maintained repository health through Git index operations, and used JAX tracking analysis to identify padding interference issues in action losses. Impact: Enables AI agents to safely consume tool outputs without causing JSON-RPC corruption, eliminates repository redundancy of metadata, and clarifies optimization paths for training stability. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Integrated Research Scout and Profiler into a single CLI, extended Semantic Scholar citation graph API, implemented multi-source academic routing, and generated CLAUDE documents for agents. Implementation Methods: Extended parameter parser to include cascading sub-commands, implemented HTTP/XML parsing pipelines for bioRxiv/PubMed, separated bibliometric sorting from relevance scoring, and built a bilingual architecture guide. Impact: Standardized developer workflows into a unified research pipeline, enriched paper discovery reports with impact metrics without affecting analytical objectivity, and reduced onboarding resistance for downstream automated agents. tianhe Completed Work: Archived old v4 benchmark code base, designed v5 error skill quota scheduling architecture, generated Stack task demonstration videos via direct state injection, and fixed the LeRobot to PI05 converter pipeline. Implementation Methods: Performed targeted file migration through cross-file import audits, adjusted policy_adapter inheritance dependencies, shifted simulation phase detection from open-loop action replay to real state check, and corrected scalar-to-vector broadcasting issues in dataset loaders. Impact: Ensured a clean v5 execution environment on GPU nodes, achieved accurate visualization of each skill in physical simulations, and eliminated silent training failures caused by tensor dimension mismatch and environmental dependency changes. Today’s work integrated efforts across devices, unified Research Scout/Profiler CLI with citation graphs and MCP, performed strategic archiving of v4 benchmark old code, designed v5 error skill architecture, resolved key mismatches between VLA training tensor shape and environment ABI, and fixed system-level git health and localization errors, thereby stabilizing the deployment pipeline.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy 🔄 Error recovery benchmark v4 archiving and v5 architecture transition — Achieved a strategic shift from physical force injection to quota-driven Error Skill pattern; archived approximately 50 old modules through import tracking isolation and inline orphan classes; designed offline trajectory scanning, context replay engine, and strict E1-E11 boundary documentation. ✅ Integration of Research Scout + Profiler CLI and citation graph integration — Merged overlapping research scripts into a single entry point, added configuration/reference sub-commands, implemented Semantic Scholar forward/backward citation parsing, achieved multi-backend LLM routing through evaluation pipelines, separated bibliometric impact from core relevance scoring to prevent popularity bias. ✅ Integration of Gadget Framework MCP server and CalendarPro — Built an independent MCP server with strict stdout/stdin JSON-RPC isolation via a context manager, redefined output patterns to directly return content, and integrated the server into a scheduled coordination workflow. ✅ Fixing VLA/RoboTwin training pipelines and data pattern alignment — Fixed the LeRobot to PI05 converter to extract and serialize missing progress metrics; corrected pi0.py aux_targets tensor shape broadcasting issues by using explicit vector wrapping and connections instead of redundant indexes; resolved torchvision/curobo ABI mismatches through explicit version locking and CUDA extension reconstruction. ✅ Generating Stack task demonstration and MuJoCo physics engine mapping — Developed custom simulation replay scripts for Stack task error skills; diagnosed and resolved critical phase detection drift caused by YAML body_name mismatch, added _main suffix and implemented dynamic fallback mapping in engine wrappers. • MIHD spatial transcriptomics cross-sample retrieval diagnosis — Conducted parallel PCA raw features and HVG intersection baseline experiments to diagnose cross-section patch retrieval failures; determined that independent feature selection and fitting are the root cause of incompatible coordinate systems, shifting focus to joint alignment or dimension extension strategies. Implementation and Fixes ✅ System environment health and localization error fixes — Fixed daily summary _finalized logic by adding backward-compatible tolerances for old state keys; cleaned 153 macOS ._* and .DS_Store files from git indexes, updated incremental build scripts; added LC_ALL=C prefix for BSD sed branch to resolve Chinese character localization failures. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Missing _finalized boolean key for old export logs, leading to infinite pipeline merge loops during daily summary processing. Solution: Modified dictionary defaults to return True for backward compatibility, added explicit target_date filter to prevent old entries from being processed again, and unified state flag expectations across all modules. Key Insight: Serialization pipelines that handle historical data must enforce explicit defensive defaults; implicit boolean conversion leads to silent infinite loops or state being skipped in merge logic.
2. LeRobot converter converts scalar floats into vectorized feature formats, while pi0.py uses excessive JAX indices, causing auxiliary targets to expand to (b, 1, 1), resulting in cascading shape mismatch issues during VLA training. Solution: Wrapped feature output in an explicit array to meet loader format requirements, replaced jnp.stack broadcasting operations with axis-aligned connections, and adjusted pyproject dependencies to remove expired C++ ABI residues.
Key Insight: Data loading formats must strictly comply with downstream tensor order requirements; without a clear reconstruction mechanism for target tool packages, implicit vectorization and expired binary caching continue to fail in batch training environments.
3. Cross-sample spatial transcriptomics patch retrieval returns zero results due to implicit coordinate system mismatch and scale inconsistency between parts. Solution: Adopted an independent parallel PCA fitting and shared HVG intersection baseline approach; determined that independent feature isolation fundamentally destroys comparability, prompting the use of joint training/orthogonal alignment pipelines.
Key Insight: Independent preprocessing pipelines for cross-modal retrieval inevitably produce non-comparable spaces; a unified baseline generation or architecture-level alignment mechanism is needed before downstream fusion models can accurately evaluate them.
4. MuJoCo engine asset naming convention lags behind configuration files, causing identical position reading and open-loop action drift, completely disrupting visualization phase detection. Solution: Updated YAML config to enforce use of _main suffix, implemented dynamic fallback lookup in simulation wrappers, and replaced action propagation replay with direct real state inspection.

Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Severe document fragmentation and architectural drift cause high cognitive load; outdated descriptions of encoder size and deleted modules lead to failures during blind execution. Solution: Established a strict minimalistic document structure (4 core files), performed targeted source code cross-verification via parallel parsing proxies, removed all end-to-end references according to instructions, and implemented strict archiving rules for old guides. Key Insight: Architectural drift in machine learning projects is equivalent to a “hidden error”; systematic verification of high-level guides with underlying source code is crucial before extending features, and future-oriented user paths should replace detailed implementation directories.
2. Mixed experiment outputs blur dataset boundaries, while visualization scripts rely on implicit memory order, resulting in inconsistent spatial and real annotation. Solution: Enforced strict hierarchical separation in output directories, and replaced direct position array assignments with explicit barcode-to-index lookup dictionaries in mapping scripts to ensure stable coordinate alignment.
Key Insight: Dataset separation must be enforced at the root level during initial design, and spatial coordinates must be aligned using stable keys rather than relying on implicit order, as cache loading or file sources often reorder lines unpredictably.
3. VLA training losses fluctuate severely due to fixed-size tensor padding weakening gradient signals, combined with adjustments to auxiliary head weights disrupting core action learning. Solution: Tracked forward passes to calculate precise gradient dilution ratios; maintained low task loss weight (0.1) to preserve action flow matching, and adjusted task position weight to approximately 5.0 to counteract class imbalance without compromising main policy gradients.
Key Insight: Gradient scaling ratios must be calculated explicitly before adjusting loss weights in a flow-matching architecture; strictly shield non-padding dimensions from computation to prevent signal degradation to zero.
4. Kubernetes PID namespace isolation prevents standard GPU telemetry tools from associating visible containers with hardware metrics, while logical device remapping causes EGL rendering initialization failures on shared HPC nodes. Solution: Developed hybrid polling scripts combining psutil process visibility and nvidia-smi CSV hardware queries; injected explicit MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID coverage flags to synchronize third-party rendering backends with PyTorch logical CUDA mappings.
Key Insight: Separate process visibility from hardware telemetry in containerized environments; logical device ID mapping must be synchronized across the entire computing stack, not just main drivers, to prevent silent runtime failures.
5. Cross-platform terminal encoding errors cause replacement characters in tmux and SSH sessions, persist even when server region settings are correct. Solution: Isolated the root cause as a mismatch between local Windows client code page and remote settings; determined that using chcp 65001 or OS-level Unicode beta flags is necessary to stop unnecessary server service restarts.
Key Insight: Diagnose client input vector configuration before proposing infrastructure-level modifications that could disrupt shared user workflows.
General Issues 6. Node.js runtime proxy bypasses, conda environment splitting, editable installation issues, and bias introduced by deterministic data sampling cause distribution changes in CLI tools and preprocessing pipelines. Solution: Applied NODE_OPTIONS proxy flags to separate the undici engine from OS environment variables, used dependency override installation flags in isolated conda environments, and repaired conversion scripts to inherit random reference patterns.
Key Insight: Modern runtimes enforce strict proxy isolation for security; editable installations in split environments require explicit bypass flags, and dataset preprocessing must inherit randomness from validation periods to prevent silent data damage during fine-tuning.

During rapid architectural adjustments, excessive clarification loops often hinder the autonomy of planning patterns, requiring direct user commands to prevent recursive state rejection or overly complex initialization processes. VLA-RoboTwin critical region annotation critical_region data is all zero, τ=0.10m threshold is purely based on estimation and does not match actual working space scale [VLA-RoboTwin] (2026-03-08) Solution: Do not adjust parameters directly, instead record original ee_target_distances (4–8 distance variables per task), analyze real data distribution first before data-driven calibration of the threshold
Learning Insights Architecture- Three standard checks after large-scale implementation: (1) Whether the new service is connected to the startup chain; (2) Whether cross-layer updates (IntentType→route→handler→service) are consistent; (3) Whether silent exceptions (except: pass) hide runtime errors. Passing tests is a necessary condition rather than a sufficient one, and defects in the integration layer can only be detected through end-to-end verification. Before designing an Agentic system, actively study mature similar projects—OpenClaw’s EventBus/CronScheduler/Plugin registration pattern and GSD’s STATE.md persistent memory/multi-Agent context isolation are highly reusable architectural patterns; related fixes should be merged into a single change rather than implemented in stages to avoid code rework. apply_tree(strict=False) is an implicit risk in ML training pipelines: if new training features that need normalization are not updated simultaneously with the norm_stats calculation script, it will cause silent scale mismatch affecting training quality; the mismatch records of AI systems are free annotation data, and automatically returning them as utterance augmentations can achieve low-cost continuous self-improvement. Two-stage information processing (rough screening + fine evaluation) is better than single-stage full processing in terms of token efficiency and analysis depth: Stage 1 focuses on problem relevance/innovation/authority of source (30 seconds judgment), Stage 2 focuses on key insights driving effects rather than engineering details, and critically examines the baseline and metrics chosen by the author. Debugging Analysis of the root cause of low GPU utilization in VLA inference: action chunking makes inference calls sparse (about 8 calls per trial × 2.5 s/200 s total time = 10%); multi-client concurrency does not improve strict serial inference throughput. The correct optimization direction is BatchedVLAServer batch inference + independent deployment on multiple GPUs. Diagnostic path for BC-RNN SR=0%; first check whether the observation key name/dimensions match training, then use historical training logs to distinguish “evaluation bug” vs “training already failed” to avoid misdiagnosis as model capability issues; bare except is the most common debugging obstacle in rendering/simulation frameworks, and should be immediately changed to except Exception: traceback.print_exc(). Parameter settings should be driven by experiments rather than intuitive estimation: first collect a small amount of data to verify the actual distribution before setting thresholds; incorrect estimation of key parameters (such as distance threshold, driving version) will cause the entire batch of data to be invalid or installation failure. Tools 4-way parallel sub-Agents + the main thread handling non-parallelizable parts can control the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files within a single session; the key is dividing agent task boundaries based on non-overlapping file sets; BatchedVLAServer parallel evaluation (44 minutes/9 tasks) saves about 80% time compared to serial execution. Standard solution for fixing headless HPC nodes’ Vulkan/EGL rendering: extract a user-space GL library from the NVIDIA official .run package that strictly matches the kernel version (no need to install kernel modules), inject it via VK_ICD_FILENAMES/__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES/LD_LIBRARY_PATH, without root; EGL/Vulkan device configuration is independent of CUDA; normal CUDA performance does not mean Vulkan is available. The arXiv comment field is a de facto conference acceptance announcement area; by searching the full text with all:"CVPR 2025" and filtering after comment, a specialized search for conference papers can be achieved; au:"Author Name" AND (kw1 OR kw2) is an effective way to track specific researchers’ latest work in the system. Domain Knowledge Learning-based fusion (QFormer) is significantly better than simple concatenation: scGPT 512d representations themselves are valuable but require non-linear projection to be fully activated (+117% vs scGPT-only); STAIG’s gene encoder is decoupled from GNN training, and differences between documents and code can only be found through code tracking; zero-shot capabilities are the core competitive point against methods that rely on training. Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning reaches 95–100% on Stack-like tasks (overall 58.9%), while BC-RNN fails completely (0%); task complexity (multiple steps, fine operations) is the main factor determining the success rate gap between VLA and traditional sequence modeling; the Pi0.5 LoRA mode also requires at least 2 × 80GB GPUs (FSDP is a necessary prerequisite). AI Usage Notes Effective Patterns:
✓ Multi-layer code tracking (3–4 call stacks) accurately identifies the facts of STAIG architecture, providing evidence at the line-level, which is more reliable than document analysis. ✓ 4-way parallel Agents divide tasks based on non-overlapping file sets, enabling the large-scale migration of 65 symlink files to be completed within a single session. ✓ Systematic analysis of sacct step timestamps correctly excludes misjudgments caused by AI operations leading to NODE_FAIL, establishing a causal evidence chain. ✓ Actively clarify ambiguous requirements by AskUserQuestion (whether author search needs LLM evaluation), precisely transforming product requirements into engineering solutions. ✓ Systematically verify the correctness of experimental configurations (source of base model) with three layers of evidence, outperforming intuitive judgment. Limitations:
✗ No verification that new features are connected to the system startup chain after implementation; only relying on unit tests omits integration layer checks (BackgroundCoordinator not started). ✗ No active study of mature industry implementations when designing Agentic systems; need user clarification before referring to OpenClaw/GSD architectural patterns. ✗ Parameter settings lack experimental validation (τ=0.10m purely estimated), resulting in all critical_region labeled data being 0. ✗ Research contributions describe technical details rather than competitive advantages; the differentiated positioning of zero-shot needs user clarification. ✗ Initial task scheduling is conservative and serial, without actively identifying opportunities for parallel execution of long-term GPU tasks + lightweight visualization tasks. ✗ Lack of necessary resume/fresh-start intent confirmation before resource-intensive operations (GPU training); misstarting fresh-start overwrites checkpoints. Next Week’s Priorities Core priorities next week: 1) Fix three bugs in CalendarPro’s context-aware section (streamline general_keywords removal of confirmation words/time words + pass _llm_classify with the last 3 conversation histories + reset GENERAL route utterances), completing the final loop from architecture upgrade to actual usability; 2) Complete the visual replay logic for pre-error trajectories (storage layer ready, complete initial state playback and frame rendering in the visualization script); 3) Monitoring and evaluation of zhaoganlong training results: Diffusion Policy is expected to be completed in 2–4 days, Pi0.5 FSDP requires about 31 hours, start batch eval immediately after training; 4) Unlock LLaVA MPM training: confirm the completeness of cpx2 user’s local llava-v1.5-7b, start training by pointing to the local path with --model_name_or_path; 5) Threshold calibration for key regions in VLA-RoboTwin: after analyzing the actual distribution of ee_target_distances, reset τ value and re-collect critical_region labels; 6) Formal fix and normal task evaluation for BC-RNN observation key bug; 7) Render demonstration video (comparison of success/failure for Pi0.5 high SR tasks). Research Scout is ready, can start configuring regular paper discovery processes for MIHD, error_recovery_benchmark, etc.

Solution: Abandoned relative traversal methods and replaced them with hard-coding the absolute project root directory via environment variables sys.path.] Exposed key test files manually, recalculated parent traversal depth, and directly fixed cross-project dependency connections.
Key Insight: Direct file path resolution eliminated dangerous symbolic link indirectness; remote execution requires clear state management, and hard-coding sys.path after refactoring is crucial for maintaining a predictable evaluation tree.
2. Pipeline design enforced sequential validation, reducing computational utilization; MuJoCo/EGL device mismatch caused background Slurm job freezes; simple synthetic pulse injection failed to trigger physical failures. Solution: Shifted to parallel visual extraction via direct database queries, strictly aligned CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID in SRun commands, and adapted to use real-world error datasets instead of fragile synthetic triggering mechanisms.
Key Insight: Overlapping generation and validation optimized cluster throughput; simulation rendering context must physically match device IDs, and using existing error datasets is usually better than unstable programmatic injections.
3. Concurrent background agents and SRun tracking experienced partial write, Makefiles, and other overlapping dependency conflicts, as well as lost trajectory arrays during serialization. Solution: Coordinated phased transition from manual to agent-based handling to prevent locking conflicts, added explicit blocking calls to track jobs, and modified the I/O layer to preserve action sequences and trigger steps rather than relying solely on static snapshots.
Key Insight: Strategic scope control prevents conflicts during parallel refactoring; capturing rich process state during generation is more efficient than post-database reconstruction.

Daily Report — 2026-03-07 Overview Completed Work: Conducted a multi-field research project covering spatial transcriptomics validation, robot policy evaluation process, personal AI agent architecture, macOS desktop interface optimization, and automated literature discovery tools. Implementation Methods: Through parallel HPC cluster script writing, Swift UI component refactoring, Python process debugging, code integration, and dynamic configuration parsing chains on distributed workstations. Impact: Corrected key benchmark metric biases in the evaluation framework, achieved stable multi-task VLA/LoRA training with significant reduced computational overhead, transformed the intent-based routing mechanism into a state-based architecture, and established production-deployable standards. DCC Completed Work: Expanded MIHD spatial transcriptomics benchmark testing to the Visium HD dataset, evaluated 27 embedding methods across tissues using RM-IDEAL, fixed scGPT checkpoint loading errors, and resolved visual encoder coordinate mapping issues. Implementation Methods: Implemented WWL graph kernel computation, achieved dynamic coordinate alignment via array step analysis, enforced attribute persistence to restore corrupted weights, and used parallel synthesis agents to process structured literature. Impact: Restored ARI metrics (+44.4% improvement), verified the advantages of STAIG fusion in cross-sample domain alignment, and established reproducible histological embedding processes quantitative benchmarks. MacBook Completed Work: Implemented a web page wallpaper engine based on WKWebView that supports full browsing mode, resolved macOS sandbox network restrictions and native window routing conflicts, fixed the rendering issue of the Liquid Glass screen protector, and integrated the cross-platform Gadget CLI tool to combine historical daily reports. Implementation Methods: Configured network client permissions, raised NSWindow level from intercept.desktopWindow to interactive.normal, removed conflicting rendering masks, and designed a export/merge process with atomic write protection and early cache termination. Impact: Achieved desktop media interaction functionality consistent with macOS system standards, eliminated continuous UI transparency/network issues, and automated cross-platform static website generation and archiving processes. TzJsDesktop Completed Work: Built and deployed the CalendarPro autonomous service system (Phases 1–3), rewritten the session-aware intent classification logic, implemented dynamic token budget context compression, and expanded unit test coverage to 360+ cases. Implementation Methods: Applied phased A/B/C/D structural guidelines, replaced static keyword routing with a dual-verification dynamic classifier, integrated a mismatch-based automatic enhancement loop, and solved the BackgroundCoordinator startup bottleneck via clear dependency injection hooks. Impact: Eliminated context loss misclassification under short prompts, achieved active task discovery and long-term memory persistence, and transformed the system from passive scheduling into an self-improving autonomous agent framework. tianhe Completed Work: Fully reengineered the ErrorRecoveryBenchmark infrastructure: fixed BC-RNN metric cascade failures, optimized Phoenix/FLARE multi-GPU training using DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 and LoRA strategies, converted local HuggingFace weights to bypass agent bottlenecks, and expanded policy deployment scenario generation to 1000+ multi-task inputs. Implementation Methods: Fixed four bug cascades in collector.py/env_wrapper.py, reduced ZeRO-3 overhead, adjusted epoch size based on the verified 1M sample dataset, implemented pre-loaded numpy HDF5 worker processes, and resolved Vulkan/Slurm cgroup compatibility issues. Impact: Restored RP metrics to a credible level (0.800), compressed LLaVA training time from 13.5 days to about 2 days, achieved 8×A800 node parallel GPU utilization, and established a stable validation process for subsequent VLA policy comparisons. By developing cross-device spatial transcriptomics benchmarks, robot error recovery infrastructure, autonomous calendar architecture, desktop media functions, and research paper analysis tools, reproducible scientific benchmarks were established, accelerating the training cycle by over 80%, and unifying cross-platform deployment protocols.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy ✅ MIHD spatial transcriptomics benchmark testing and scGPT checkpoint fix — Adapted the RM-IDEAL process to Visium HD data, evaluated 27 methods and 7 layers across samples, fixed Transformer attribute loss in scGPT checkpoints (ARI improvement +44.4%), and solved visual encoder coordinate mismatch issues via mathematical mapping. 🔄 ErrorRecoveryBenchmark process fix and VLA/LoRA training optimization — Resolved BC-RNN metric distortion cascade issues (RP/SPL fields, successful coverage), optimized LLaVA MPM/MCM training by reducing ZeRO-2 level and local weight conversion, expanded multi-task scenario generation to 1000+ injections, and established parallel evaluation infrastructure. ✅ CalendarPro autonomous service architecture and context routing — Implemented Phase 1–3 architecture modifications including session-aware intent classification, token budget context compression, dynamic mismatch learning loop, and BackgroundCoordinator initialization hooks, verified via 360+ tests. ✅ MacBook WKWebView functionality and native browsing mode implementation — Designed a dynamic web wallpaper engine, resolved sandbox permissions and browsing mode window routing (.normal level transition), fixed rendering transparency and audio synchronization issues, and aligned cross-frame UI layer constraints. ✅ Two-phase evaluation and configuration system for research paper screening — Reconstructed the literature discovery process into a fast screening/deep analysis cognitive flow, implemented dynamic LLM language parsing chain (CLI > configuration), added automatic initialization from the browsing interface, and optimized arXiv search deduplication via early cache termination. ✅ Gadget CLI tool integration with cross-platform report process — Extracted a unified run_hugo_update abstraction layer for PowerShell/Bash compatibility, built an export/merge two-phase architecture with atomic write protection, fixed regular expression header alignment errors, and enabled automatic synchronization of cross-device historical daily/monthly reports. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Despite good training performance, the BC-RNN metric cascade is almost completely broken; VLA evaluation scripts fail due to WebSocket timeout during JIT compilation. Solution: Identified missing field mapping, static YAML fallback mechanism, and observation key mismatch issues (object does not match the original architecture); fixed the collector/environment modules, aligned robomimic API signatures, added ping_timeout weights in the JIT phase, and validated via unit tests/regression suites, restoring RP to 0.800. Key Insight: The integrity of the evaluation metric chain is crucial; silent observation/key mismatch or static configuration override destroy the baseline, preventing strategic conclusions.
2. LLaVA/Phoenix training severely overestimates duration (13.5 days) due to ZeRO-3 communication overhead, unverified dataset size (160K→1M actual entries), and campus agent bandwidth blocking. Solution: Downgraded to ZeRO-2 for better balance between single/dual-card memory, reduced iteration counts, adjusted batch size based on hardware, used local safetensors conversion and vocabulary alignment to bypass agents, and preloaded HDF5 into CPU RAM to avoid I/O starvation.
Key Insight: Training process optimization requires balancing computational cost and convergence thresholds; clear dataset length verification must occur before iterative computation, and local format conversion can reliably bypass restrictive network tunnels.
3. macOS sandbox blocks WKWebView network requests; .desktopWindow level intercepts all input events; the scroll bar appears transparent due to drawsBackground=false; the screen protector overlay shows a gray halo. Solution: Added network.client permissions, restored window level to interactive .normal, retained ignoresMouseEvents=false, injected Chrome User-Agent string, hidden text via CALayer instead of snapshots, and removed conflicting CSS/rendering masks.
Key Insight: Native operating system synthesis rules strictly override Web/CSS layers; interactive overlay requires higher levels than system-defined input mask boundaries, and clear permissions are essential for sandbox networks.
4. CalendarPro static keyword routing misclassifies prompt words that depend on context (“ok”, “time”); BackgroundCoordinator fails silently; insufficient test coverage hides integration faults. Solution: Implemented dual-verification dynamic routing based on session state signals, replaced silent except Exception: pass blocks with structured logs, added clear startup health check hooks, and expanded tests via parallel sub-agents (196→360+ cases).
Key Insight: Dynamic dialogue processes require state-driven classification rather than static rules; without clear lifecycle management and observability, completion does not equate to success.
5. MIHD visual encoder embedding vectors fail checkpoint loading due to tissue_positions X/Y column inversion (4th/5th column swap) and use_fast_transformer attributes never persisted, resulting in ARI close to zero. Solution: Verified coordinate swap via array step analysis, forced array_row/col mapping correction, cache cleanup, reallocated missing attributes in __init__, and triggered full embedding reconstruction in DLPFC region.
Key Insight: Spatial/biological data pipelines contain potential geometric transformations requiring statistical verification; dynamic conditions must be explicitly persisted to prevent silent weight damage during framework upgrades or configuration changes.
Human and AI Approaches Architecture Strategy and System Constraint Identification Role Method Human Prioritize overall workflow boundaries, implement phased development milestones with clear state transitions, identify physical/simulation constraints via artifact validation rather than logs, require concise process structures that align with user intent. AI Adopt continuous integration patterns, perform comprehensive environment simulation (e.g., using only Slurm rules), use defensive adapter stacking, and flat batch processing; requires clear boundary constraints or structural refactoring instructions to converge on optimal system design. Analysis of Differences: Human reasoning focuses on system architecture, platform hard boundaries, and strategic resource topology; AI optimizes local execution and technical integrity, adjusting only when constrained or guided by phased paradigms.
Training Optimization and Compute Resource Management Role Method Human Early identification of timeline mismatch and return on investment issues (13.5 days), forced downgrade to ZeRO-2 and manual iteration adjustment, prioritized use of local cache artifacts over agent troubleshooting, implemented strict GPU allocation boundaries to maintain cluster stability. AI Initially generated a process that is academically complete but costly; via iterative adjustment of environment variables, CLI flags, and network diagnostics, shifted to efficient hardware routing strategies after explicit user intervention. Analysis of Differences: Human oversight avoids significant computational waste through early strategic interventions based on timeline awareness and cluster topology knowledge; AI first optimizes technical syntax, requiring user adjustment to match business/research cycles.

Solution: Replaced SwiftUI material sampling with a clear NSVisualEffectView mask, injected it strictly at the host layer; rewritten access lifecycle, tightly bound safe range bookmarks to application start/terminate phases, and distinguished NSOpenPanel tokens from persistent storage paths. Key Insight: Native window combos cannot be penetrated by advanced UI abstraction unless explicit layer injection is done; operating system permission protection requires definite lifecycle binding, not relying on runtime fallback mechanisms.

AI Rapidly generates execution frameworks, dependency graphs, and batch evaluation pipelines, but initially tends to adjust parameters rather than analyze root causes, assumes checkpoints are ready without verification of artifacts, and struggles to correlate independent modules with downstream data routing needs. Analysis: Humans are responsible for defining strategic scope, risk grading, and domain validation; AI excels in large-scale execution and structure generation, but requires clear architectural boundaries and real-time state verification to avoid output mismatch or prompt bypass issues.
Limitations of AI Key Limitations Lack of deep pre-training on HPC network isolation strategies, framework memory allocation features, and silent environment assumptions, often requiring multiple rounds of artifact validation to resolve infrastructure conflicts. General Limitations Without static analysis, difficult to handle long-term pipeline context mapping and complex code library data flow reasoning, often falling into repetitive planning loops or generating outputs that do not align with real-time repository metrics. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Base model evaluation must clearly distinguish baseline success rates from error recovery capabilities; accurate training/ evaluation state alignment and strict memory boundary control are crucial for eliminating silent configuration failures in complex deployment stacks. Implementation and Fixes ✅ Error Recovery Dependency List and Documentation Integration — Structured markdown format for non-internal conda environments, HDF5 datasets, and system scripts, and referenced with the main project summary to ensure repeatability of benchmarks and eliminate documentation ambiguity. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. The base model workflow silently ignored key gene encoder embeddings, while the macOS API reduced functionality without explicit permissions, leading to inconsistent scientific baselines and continuous application freezes. Solution: Deeply traced the trainer architecture, shifted evaluation strategies to validated fusion techniques, added mandatory Apple plist permissions and secure URL lifecycle hooks to restore sandbox compliance.
Key Insight: When AI models and operating system security frameworks are misconfigured, they default to fallback states; structured code audits and strict list validation are needed, not surface-level debugging.
2. VLA inference workflows experienced severe GPU starvation (about 10% utilization) during evaluation tests due to Action Chunking idle gaps, WebSocket serialization bottlenecks, and TCP connection switching overhead. Solution: Analyzed latency distribution to confirm CPU/IO dominance, then designed BatchedVLAServer, using timer-based queuing, sequential GPU routing, and subprocess work threads to mask serialization issues and achieve true parallel throughput.
Key Insight: Hardware efficiency in RL/VLA evaluations depends on workflow concurrency and data flow architecture, not raw accelerator computing power; scaling requires independent hardware isolation per GPU, not client多重 processing.
3. Shared HPC clusters experienced severe scheduling timeout issues under load, plus excessive JAX/XLA usage of VRAM and parallel MuJoCo simulations caused GPU fragmentation and process-level deadlocks. Solution: Implemented direct file system log parsing instead of interactive SLURM queries, executed XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.85 buffer management, isolated work threads via osmesa, and separated the training process into independent job steps.
Key Insight: Infrastructure visibility and stability require parallel hardware diagnosis and explicit process isolation; traditional schedulers or shared rendering contexts cannot solve resource allocation issues during computational saturation.
General Issues 4. Automatic network extraction failed to address modern SwiftUI documentation for JavaScript rendering, and hard-coded environment scripts caused shell escape syntax errors and inconsistent evaluation targets during initial cluster deployment. Solution: Shifted focus to direct GitHub repositories and native source code references to confirm API signatures, generated optimized string escapes via dynamic scripts, and ensured strict domain checkpoint alignment before workflow activation.
Key Insight: On JavaScript-intensive platforms, the reliability of external documentation extraction drops significantly; direct source code review is required; automatic deployment scripts must dynamically parse environment variables and verify target ranges before execution to prevent cache context drift.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Scientific Benchmark Strategy and Architecture Correction Role Method Human Provide high-level milestones and metric requirements, while assuming the existing fusion configuration is correct; require constraint-based debugging when parallel execution fails. AI Actively map experiments, identify fundamental code defects that hinder scientific effectiveness, shift to accurate QFormer evaluations, and iterate resource patches until optimization is achieved via architecture adjustments. Difference Analysis: Humans define strategic endpoints and adjust scope offsets based on domain constraints; AI performs deep structural diagnosis, avoids methodological false positives, and makes corresponding implementation adjustments.
Cluster Workflow Adjustment: Direct Resource Control vs. Traditional Automation Method Description Direct Resource Control Adjust resource allocation for specific needs. Traditional Automation Depends on shared rendering context and conventional schedulers. —— —— Human Prioritize fast, practical SSH access to the same computing node, rather than traditional task queuing; explicitly bypass old automation rules when they hinder operational efficiency. AI Uses hard-coded HPC scheduling rules for stability, relies on sequential queue management, and requires real-time fault feedback before adapting to direct node interaction standards. Difference Analysis: Humans treat clusters as flexible resource pools, enhancing infrastructure flexibility and rapid iteration; AI seeks balance between security and conventions until tools and actual network topology are clearly adjusted.
VLA Optimization Architecture Mapping and Low-Level Analysis Comparison Role Method Human Conceptually maps multi-threaded pipelines, identifies specific bottlenecks in sequential loops, and pauses work before expansion to perform basic GPU analysis. AI Converts concurrent strategies into executable Python server logic, evaluates client limitations, studies related literature, and integrates implementation blueprints that align with new strategic directions. Difference Analysis: Humans provide architectural boundaries and bottleneck identification; AI provides low-level code templates, execution mechanisms, empirical analyses, and structured research outcomes to validate proposed optimization paths.
macOS Security Debugging and UI Constraint Enforcement Role Method Human Provide precise console logs, reveal unmonitored fallback behaviors, and explicitly limit screen saver design to achieve native transparent rendering without background cards. AI Isolates missing permission configurations, rewrites core API hooks for different window managers, and overpursuits backward compatibility before UI constraints are received, leading to initial implementation failures. Difference Analysis: Console evidence connects high-level logic to operating system security boundaries; humans enforce strict visual constraints, while AI converts operational instructions into producible code architecture.
AI Limitations Key Limitations Default use of mature HPC scheduling templates and JAX resource heuristics exhibits convention preferences, until direct failure or explicit adjustment forces architecture transformation. General Limitations Maintaining reliable state and parsing accuracy in large-scale sequential CLI execution and large CSV outputs is difficult; despite strong initial diagnostic capabilities, recovery of context or auxiliary scripts is often required. Execution stability is poor when handling complex string escaping, real-time cluster state verification under high load, and silent operating system API degradation without list validation; iterative fallback strategies are needed. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Basic biostatistical models cannot exceed statistical baselines on raw data; advanced downstream fusion techniques are required to unlock predictive spatial embedding and validate scientific claims. Infrastructure visibility on shared clusters needs parallel hardware diagnosis, not reliance on schedulers; true VLA/ML pipelines should focus on data flow concurrency and model-level speculation decoding, not merely on computational scale expansion. Actively updating proxy configurations and operation memory to match evolving infrastructure preferences is more effective than relying on static automation templates or document assumptions for complex benchmark workflows. When permissions lack explicit keys, Apple security APIs implicitly degrade to insecure fallback behaviors; strict list validation and robust runtime lifecycle management are necessary to ensure sandbox compliance. AI analysis of EnvironmentMismatchError revealed that the 649 scenario library contained two types of environments (~519 compatible + ~130 natural_* incompatible). collector.py added a scene-level try-except to fix it, and the actual valid evaluation scenarios are about 519. 🔄 Built and started the parallel fine-tuning pipeline for Pi0.5 LoRA 9 tasks (2026-03-01) — Created train_pi05_benchmark.py (5 sub-commands), registered 18 configurations in openpi/config.py, and fixed 4 startup bugs (JAX_PLATFORMS, norm_stats path, boolean parameters, W&B agent), starting successfully with 6×A800, 100% GPU utilization, and 77.7GB/card. 🔄 Implemented the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline script and started parallel training for 9 tasks (2026-02-28) — Implemented train_bc_rnn_benchmark.py based on hyperparameters from the MimicGen paper, fixed 3 library-level bugs (mujoco_py import, MimicGen environment registration, inheritance chain in get_bounding_box_half_size), and parallelized 9 tasks on a single GPU (~2.2GB VRAM/task), including 50 rollout evaluations every 20 epochs. ✅ Identified and fixed the missing object observation keys in Coffee BC-RNN (2026-03-01) — By comparing the actual obs key structure of the HDF5 dataset, it was found that Coffee lacks 57-dimensional object states (Pod/Machine/Holder position + relative pose + hinge angle). Added extra_low_dim=['object'] for all 9 tasks, fixing the root cause of 0% SR in Coffee. ✅ Identified and fixed the root cause of 0% success rate in Pi0.5 evaluation (2026-02-26) — Confirmed that the training task (MimicGen 5 task) and the evaluation task (PickPlace) do not overlap at all; changed to evaluate on the training task. Human analysis directly pointed out the issue, and the AI’s initial analysis failed to identify this most obvious cause immediately. ✅ Rewritten the BC-RNN image mode configuration (5 tasks, consistent with MimicGen paper) (2026-02-26) — Rewritten all bc_rnn_configs from low_dim to image mode: ResNet18 + SpatialSoftmax encoder, CropRandomizer 76×76, RNN hidden_dim 1000, batch_size 16, epoch_every_n_steps 500, consistent with the main results of the MimicGen paper. ✅ Implemented three CPU acceleration methods for MIHD fusion training (2026-02-23) — Replaced scipy cdist vectorization with O(n²) nested loops (~100–500x), migrated random number generation to GPU to eliminate per-epoch transmission overhead, and added a batch forward interface to QFormerFusion (expected 20–50x). ✅ Developed the pipeline for generating error scenarios in BC-RNN Stack_D0 (2026-03-01) — Fixed four consecutive bugs in accessing image observations in robomimic BC-RNN (enable_camera detection, json.loads parsing checkpoint config, automatic detection of 84×84 resolution, HWC→CHW transpose + normalization), generating 11 tip_over error scenarios and MP4 visualizations. ✅ Full evaluation of RM-IDEAL across 27 embedding methods × 7 layers (2026-02-28) — Ran the full RM-IDEAL evaluation with 27 embedding methods, generated 189 three-panel visualizations for Zhang, and staig_fusion ranked first with an average r=0.396 (peak r=0.644 at Layer_3), quantifying the advantage of multi-modal fusion. ✅ Extended the evaluation framework to 5 MimicGen tasks (2026-02-26) — Created 5 new task YAML configs + task_registry.yaml, added --task parameter to the 1/3/4 scripts, fixed the observation dimension error caused by _D0 env suffix stripping (65→37), and rewritten run_full_eval.sh to support multi-task loops. ✅ Full slice benchmark for STAIG fusion (11 DLPFC slices) (2026-02-23) — Ran pca+uni2+staig_fusion and none+uni2+staig_fusion on 11 DLPFC slices, fixed the UNI2 patch_size compatibility bug (256×256→224×224), with success in 10/11 slices and an average ARI=0.546; known collapse at 151676. ✅ Comparison experiment between MIHD Vision Refine and Baseline (2026-02-23) — Ran full comparisons of 8 fusion methods with/without scan_cluster refine on slice 151673, and qformer+no-refine was optimal (ARI=0.4832). Found that refine is beneficial for weak fusion (attention +0.086) but harmful for strong fusion (qformer -0.054). ✅ Fixed key bugs in evaluate_mimicgen.py and collector.py (2026-02-23) — Fixed the in-place array modification bug in quat2axisangle (used np.clip+copy), captured EnvironmentMismatchError at the scene level in collector.py, ensured reproducibility with env.seed(), and verified the 8D state dimension assert. Issues and Solutions 1. Pi0.5 full fine-tuning training requires ~62GB/GPU, and JAX FSDP=4 cannot effectively reduce VRAM (only slicing storage does not reduce activation memory), repeatedly causing OOM [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Switch to the gemma_2b_lora+gemma_300m_lora architecture, reducing training parameters by ~90% and reducing VRAM to ~22.5GB/GPU. Job 46553 runs stably at 2.0s/step.
2. All three-way evaluations of M14 crashed on scene 122/649: ~130 natural_* scenario XML hashes are incompatible with the current Mimicgen environment, triggering EnvironmentMismatchError without detection, causing the entire evaluation process to crash [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Add a try-except for EnvironmentMismatchError in collector.py’s collect_on_scenes()for each scene, skip incompatible scenarios and log warnings, and restart with–resume`. The actual valid evaluation scenarios are about 519.
3. Training logs are severely distorted due to stdout buffering: Pi0.5 training shows only ~580 steps, but actually reached step 3000, leading to misjudged training termination and unnecessary restart [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-23) Solution: Add PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1+stdbuf -oL to the training script and sbatch submission scripts; use sbatch for long-term training and decouple the independent batch job from the interactive session lifecycle.
4. The success rate of Pi0.5 evaluation is 0%, misjudged as model quality issues [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-26) Solution: Confirmed that the training task (MimicGen 5 task) and the evaluation task (PickPlace) do not overlap at all; change to evaluating on the training tasks (Coffee/Stack/Threading/Assembly).
5. Observation dimension mismatch in BC-RNN evaluation (Expected 65, got 37) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-26) Solution: Add a import mimicgen registration for the _D0 environment in create_env(); stop stripping the _D0 suffix and retain all MimicGen observables (_D0 environment provides additional object state observables).
6. scGPT TransformerModel.__init__ omits self.use_fast_transformer, causing the key remapping in load_pretrained() to never execute, and 17.7% attention weights are randomly initialized; strict=False silently skips without error [MIHD] (2026-02-28) Solution: Add a single line self.use_fast_transformer = use_fast_transformer in model.py. After fixing, ARI improved by 44.4%, and all 11 DLPFC slice embeddings were extracted again.
7. WebSocket client always reports ConnectionRefusedError; attempts with different address formats (localhost/127.0.0.1/0.0.0.0) all fail [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-28) Solution: Found that the http_proxy environment variable is set to 127.0.0.1:10087; the websockets library fails due to connection through the proxy.After unsetting all proxy variables at the beginning of run_eval.sh, the connection was established successfully.
8. CoffeeMachineBodyObject lacks the get_bounding_box_half_size() method, causing an AttributeError during the initialization of the MimicGen Coffee task rollout (An interface gap between MimicGen and the current robosuite version) [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-02-28)Solution: Trace the entire call chain (coffee_machine.py→CoffeeMachineBodyObject→CompositeBodyObject→MujocoXMLObject), and implement get_bounding_box_half_size() in three different base classes. 9. The HD data uns[‘spatial’] image is a full-resolution image, but its coordinates are in the cropped fullres pixel space, resulting in a mismatch during visualization; moreover, since X has been logged transformed, the pipeline will again normalize_total+log1p, causing a double transformation [MIHD] (2026-02-28) Solution: Replace the uns[‘spatial’] image with cropped_fullres.tif in load_hd_data() and recalculate the scalefactor; add the skip_log parameter to preprocess_data(), and pass skip_log=True for HD data only for HVG filtering.
10. The Coffee BC-RNN loss converges normally (-7.66→-15.4), but SR remains 0% all the time. With the same configuration, epoch 20 already reaches 64%, showing a high similarity to insufficient model capacity [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: Compare with the actual obs key structure of the HDF5 dataset, and find that Coffee requires a 57-dimensional object state (required for multi-stage precise operations), and the configuration template lacks this field; add extra_low_dim=[‘object’] for all 9 tasks and regenerate the configuration.
11. The robomimic BC-RNN image observation access fails at four consecutive levels: the detection logic of enable_camera/checkpoint config is in JSON string format/image resolution acquisition/HWC→CHW format conversion all have issues [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: ① Detect the rgb modality from the JSON string of checkpoint config (needs json.loads); ② Read the actual 84×84 size from shape_metadata; ③ Manually transpose HWC→CHW and convert uint8→float32/255 normalization (ObsUtils.process_obs automatically handles it in the standard rollout).
12. Pi0.5 LoRA training starts with four consecutive blocking bugs: ① Setting JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu separately is ineffective; ② Wrong path for norm_stats; ③ Boolean parameter–overwrite=False is ineffective; ④ Access to W&B external network on HPC nodes is blocked [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: ① Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu simultaneously; ② The actual path for norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json; ③ Use–no-overwrite instead; ④ Predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled.
13. VisiumHD HD data pipeline path adaptation: The image path lookup in the vision encoder and spatial coords loading during fusion fail because they assume the DLPFC directory structure [MIHD] (2026-03-01) Solution: Add the cropped_fullres.tif pattern recognition to find_spatial_image(); pass the crop_dir.parent as data_root when calling the vision encoder; directly load coordinates from adata.obsm[‘spatial’] during fusion to bypass path lookup.
14. When calculating norm_stats, GPU util=0 but memory is fully used, and the task progresses slowly for a long time; the root cause is that PaligemmaTokenizer loads eagerly on all visible GPUs when calling get_config().model [Error Recovery Benchmark] (2026-03-01) Solution: Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu simultaneously; ② The actual path for norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json; ③ Use–no-overwrite instead; ④ Predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled.
15. Architecture (architecture) JAX FSDP only splits parameter storage, which does not affect the full model loading and forward activation memory during initialization; the full training state of Pi0.5 requires ~62GB/GPU, and a single A800 with 80GB cannot support full fine-tuning; LoRA (gemma_2b_lora) is the only viable solution for the A800 cluster, reducing memory demand to ~22.5GB. When the warning “Can’t reduce memory use below 62.46GiB” appears, switch to LoRA immediately. The observation keys in BC-RNN configurations must match task complexity: Tasks like Coffee requiring multi-stage precise operations need a 57-dimensional object state, and a 84×84 image cannot provide sufficient spatial precision; the behavior of configuration bugs (normal loss but SR=0) is highly similar to insufficient model capacity, and differentiation requires comparison with dataset structures. Vectorization and batching accelerate significantly: O(n²) nested loops → cdist matrix operation approximately 100–500x, Python逐spot loops → batch GPU forward预计 20–50x. The calculation of norm_stats completely does not require model inference; forcing CPU mode + subsampling + parallelization can reduce the time from 10+ minutes to 2.5 minutes. Methodology for refactoring large repositories: Systematically grep to verify all imported dependencies → execute in the order of “create new module→update references→delete old files” → dry-run verification; before merging multiple functions with the same name, carefully compare boundary conditions (> vs >= vs < can lead to completely opposite functions). Debugging (debugging) PyTorch model.load_state_dict(strict=False) silently ignores mismatched keys, and key weights may run as random values for a long time without reporting any errors; production code should actively print missing_keys/unexpected_keys and verify parameter value statistics. Similar bugs may exist in upstream open-source repositories, and the weight loading path needs active auditing rather than blind trust. Key details of robomimic BC-RNN inference: Checkpoint config is stored as a JSON string (needs json.loads, not direct dict access); when bypassing the standard rollout process, manually transpose HWC→CHW and convert uint8→float32/255 normalization (ObsUtils.process_obs automatically handles it in the standard rollout). Domain knowledge (domain) Key conclusion from M14: BC-RNN SR=0.28%, Pi0/Pi0.5 SR=0%, and Random’s Recovery Progress (0.0199) is higher than all learning strategies—learning strategies suffer from serious distribution external generalization failure in error injection scenarios, directly proving the necessity of LoRA fine-tuning in M15. The 649 scenario database consists of two types of environments: ~519 impulse/augmented compatible scenarios (xml_hash matching) and ~130 natural_* natural capture scenarios (xml_hash different). Approximately 519 actual valid evaluation scenarios exist in M14, and all document and target episode counts need corresponding updates. STAIG fusion leads comprehensively in RM-IDEAL evaluation (average r=0.396 for 151673, peak r=0.644 for Layer_3), and multi-modal fusion has a much better ability to capture spatial niche structures than single-modal baselines (gene/vision avg r≈0.06–0.12). Vision Refine performance is polarized: beneficial for weak fusion (attention +0.086 ARI), harmful for strong fusion (qformer -0.054); strong fusion already has the ability to handle high-dimensional inputs, and dimensionality reduction loses information. Cross-task evaluation is a common trap in robot learning: Non-overlap between training set tasks and evaluation tasks directly leads to 0% SR; ensure train/eval task consistency during experimental design. The MimicGen _D0 environment provides additional object observables; removing the _D0 suffix reduces the observation dimension from 65 to 37, breaking input consistency during inference. VisiumHD coordinate mapping: r_big//4 of 2um bin gives 8um grid row (same for col); the spatial visualization size parameter in scanpy is a multiple of spot_diameter_fullres; HD 8μm (diameter≈7.3) requires size≈4.0, DLPFC (diameter≈144) uses size=1.0; the Leiden community found that (resolution=1.0) is the default clustering strategy for unlabeled HD data (crop10large k=17, Silhouette=0.302). Tools (tools) Best practices for Slurm cluster training engineering: Long-term training requires using sbatch (not srun to avoid session timeout due to SIGTERM); standardize all training scripts with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1+stdbuf -oL; clean zombie GPU processes with fuser /dev/nvidiaX before starting (monitoring tools like nvitop also hold CUDA context); MUJOCO_EGL_DEVICE_ID corresponds to the physical GPU number rather than the logic of CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Key configurations for JAX/Pi0.5 training: ① Set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""+JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu in CPU mode; ② XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.95 is effective for A800 80GB (61→77.7GB); ③ HPC nodes must predefine WANDB_MODE=disabled; ④ Use–no-overwrite for argparse boolean flags, not–flag=False; ⑤ The path for openpi norm_stats is assets//benchmark//norm_stats.json. The HTTP/HTTPS proxy environment variable (http_proxy) is transparently proxied by the Python websockets library, so unset the proxy variable when debugging local services on HPC clusters. The MimicGen environment registers via the side effect of import mimicgen in robosuite; explicit execution of this import is required before calling external tools. Fixing methods missing in third-party libraries must be implemented in the entire inheritance chain across all base classes, and fixing only the recently called point will cause errors in other subclasses. The pam_slurm_adopt cluster GPU nodes do not support direct SSH; srun –overlap can attach new steps to existing interactive jobs to reuse node resources; robomimic in a non-TTY environment will exit with EOFError if a checkpoint directory already exists, so clean the directory thoroughly before each start. summary: This week, two main tracks—space transcriptomics (MIHD) and robot error recovery benchmark—were advanced in parallel on both DCC and Tianhe clusters. On DCC, the bug related to fatal weight loading in scGPT was fixed (average ARI improvement of 44.4%), the MIHD benchmark was extended to the Visium HD dataset, and a large-scale repository refactoring of approximately 250K lines of code was completed; on Tianhe, the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline training pipeline was established from scratch (9 tasks run in parallel), the root cause of the 0% success rate in the Pi0.5 evaluation was identified and fixed, key conclusions were obtained for the M14 baseline evaluation (the learning strategy achieves SR≈0 in error scenarios, proving the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning), and the Pi0.5 LoRA 9 task was successfully fine-tuned in parallel on 6×A800 with stable operation.
title: Weekly Summary 2026-W09

content:
Daily Report — 2026-03-01 Overview of Daily Work Completed Work: Coordinated development efforts across multiple domains, including optimization of spatial transcriptomics workflows, benchmark training for embodied intelligence, development of scheduling tools, and design of cross-platform log architectures. Focus was on diagnosing invisible runtime failures, strictly enforcing framework alignment standards, and conducting comprehensive repository refactoring to eliminate technical debt. Implementation Methods: Utilized aggressive GPU resource isolation and parallel CPU preprocessing to overcome hardware bottlenecks; designed a symmetric finalize/merge state machine for log aggregation; implemented clear coordinate scaling and checkpoint persistence patches; automatically synchronized structured documents on distributed workstations. Impact: Eliminated invisible model convergence degradation and VRAM usage issues, accelerated multi-modal fusion and robot training efficiency by restoring key alignment constraints, and established a reliable cross-device workflow foundation, significantly improving architectural consistency and long-term maintainability. DCC Completed Work: Completed optimization of MIHD spatial transcriptomics workflows, including reconfiguration of scGPT checkpoints, vectorization for STAIG fusion, and coordinate mapping for Visium HD. Focus was on high-throughput model training, visual generation, and repository refactoring to support multi-modal architectures. Implementation Methods: Applied clear property persistence hooks for Transformer initialization; forced CPU vectorized edge weight computation; dynamically adjusted hires-to-full-res coordinates via scaling functions; systematically archived old dependencies using dependency graph analysis. Impact: Restored spatial encoding accuracy (ARI) in all 11 DLPFC regions from near zero to >0.54; accelerated fusion training processes 100–500 times; eliminated abandoned code paths that previously caused inference path breaks. Daily Report — 2026-02-23 General Overview Completed Tasks: Identified and resolved major serialization bottlenecks in the visual encoder fusion process, removed restrictive hard-coded constraints to support flexible multi-model benchmarks, stabilized large-scale robot policy data collection and long-term training processes, and avoided silent crashes and environment mismatches. Implementation Methods: Implemented sparse matrix vectorization, dynamic scaling adapters, and batch Transformer inference to improve performance; optimized the data collector’s fault-tolerant log skipping; updated Slurm launch scripts with non-buffered I/O, clear recovery checkpoints, and error capture mechanisms; automated statistical benchmark data reporting using defensive scipy alternatives. Impact: Initialization/training speed of complex fusion models increased by more than 20 times, enabling unrestricted cross-encoder evaluation across 11 spatial transcriptomics sections, maintaining continuous evaluation processes under 649 parallel scenarios, and allowing continuous monitoring and precise synchronization of metrics during multi-hour policy training. DCC Completed Tasks: Performed pipeline orchestration, iterative refactoring, background benchmark execution, and comparative visualization generation for the MIHD framework. Implementation Methods: Utilized AI-assisted code editing, Python syntax validation, dynamic cache management, and Bash task monitoring; integrated experimental outputs into structured CSV format and spatial plots. Impact: Achieved direct running optimization without external dependencies, maintained conda environment consistency during refactoring cycles, and provided actionable clustering insights for downstream preprocessing strategies. tianhe Completed Tasks: Coordinated parallel SLURM workloads for M14/M16 baseline analysis, VLA evaluation recovery, and Pi0.5 Phoenix LoRA training recovery. Implementation Methods: Applied targeted patches to collector.py to achieve graceful error handling; updated the training shell script with state persistence and non-buffered output flags; automated version tracking and milestone synchronization via file modifications. Impact: Eliminated pipeline interruptions caused by mixed scenario fingerprint mismatches, ensured continuous training without silent exits, and maintained cross-project version consistency without manual intervention. Key CPU and architecture optimizations were applied to the multi-omics fusion workflow, resolving environment fingerprint conflicts that caused large-scale robot evaluation interruptions, and stabilized long-term policy training through resilient monitoring and checkpoint strategies.
Tasks Architecture and Strategy 🔄 Long-term Policy Training Stability and Recovery Logic — Restored Pi0.5 Phoenix LoRA training via clear checkpoint recovery, non-buffered stdout wrapping, and SLURM error capture mechanisms; corrected evaluation environment initialization and quaternion processing to ensure reproducible state tracking. ✅ Fusion Pipeline CPU Optimization and Architecture Decoupling — Resolved O(n²) edge weight loops, sequential spot-level Transformer calls, and old cache interference; removed hard-coded UNI encoder restrictions, allowing dynamic selection of visual variant paths in the MIHD framework. ✅ Large-scale Evaluation Recovery and Fingerprint Conflict Resolution — Diagnosed EnvironmentMismatchError crashes during natural/pulse scenario collection, implemented defensive log skipping in the data collector, and successfully restored parallel Pi0/Pi0.5 evaluations for 649 scenarios. ✅ Cross-encoder Benchmark Testing and Optimization Trade-off Analysis — Performed large-scale staig_fusion tests on all 11 DLPFC regions, compared baseline and scan_cluster optimization metrics, and recorded performance differences—while dimensionality reduction benefits apply to simple fusion, they negatively impact high-capacity learners. ✅ Statistical Benchmark Report and Pipeline Restart — Executed m14_cpu baseline analysis including Fleiss’ kappa reliability test and Kruskal-Wallis discriminant test, added defensive handling for degraded scipy inputs, and updated project documentation to v4.12 version. Issues and Solutions Key Issues 1. Serialization bottlenecks in fusion loops (nested Python loops for edge weights, sequential forward processing) and hard-coded architecture restrictions caused severe CPU/GPU idleness and limited multi-encoder flexibility. Solution: Replaced iterative calculations with NumPy/scipy vectorization, filled variable-length neighbor tensors for native GPU parallelism, solved ViT patch incompatibility through dynamic scaling, and decoupled routing from strict encoder dependencies.
Key Insight: Graph-based preprocessing and sample-level Transformer inference are essentially serialized; unified tensor filling enables full batch parallelism. Traditional architectures often limit modern multi-model pipelines unless explicitly decoupled at the routing layer.
2. The mixed dataset collection pipeline crashed fatally due to inconsistent XML hashes between generated and natural scenarios, while long-term training scripts silent exited due to Python output buffering and missing checkpoint logic. Solution: Inserted EnvironmentMismatchError fallback mechanisms in the collector to log warnings and gracefully skip incompatible initialization; updated launch scripts with PYTHONUNBUFFERED flag, clear recovery flags, error capture mechanisms, and reliable evaluation environment initialization.
Key Insight: Mixed data pipelines require conditional fault tolerance rather than strict mismatch interruption protocols. Multi-hour GPU workloads need defensive I/O configuration, persistent state tracking, and reproducible environment initialization to handle preemption or silent failures.
General Issues 3. Statistical analysis failed on degraded group inputs (zero variance/single group cases), default initial spatial visualization output was a single panel rather than a comparison layout, requiring manual correction. Solution: Wrapped scipy statistical calls with defensive variance checks, returning valid default dictionaries; corrected plotting prompts to enforce multi-panel comparison structures, and automatically cached results.
Key Insight: Automated scientific pipelines must anticipate edge-case inputs and provide fallback distributions, with explicit enforcement of output format constraints during program generation.
Human and AI Approaches Strategic Level Strategic task decomposition, runtime orchestration, and pipeline automation | Roles | Methods | |——|——| | Human | Defined structured priority queues for multiple milestone dependencies (M13/M14/M16), manually verified scenario counts, mapped bottlenecks to optimizers, and inferred trade-offs in visual optimization metric representation. | | AI | Performed automatic dependency verification, dynamic file path checks, parallel CLI task allocation, applied defensive code patches for mismatched environments and statistical edge cases, and maintained real-time documentation synchronization without manual intervention. |

Obsolete compilation cache artifacts and TaskOutput API timeouts hinder real-time progress visibility, necessitating manual file system cleanup and backup filesystem checks during real-time refactoring and long-background polling. Lessons Learned Key Experiences Visual embedding optimization improved clustering performance in simple fusion, but caused performance degradation in high-capacity learners due to information loss; downstream model compatibility must be dynamically verified to prevent hidden bypasses or shape mismatches. Large-scale physical simulation and multi-hour GPU training processes require defensive fault tolerance: gracefully skip logs for different environment fingerprints, combined with clear checkpoint persistence and non-buffered standard output, to ensure observability during latent failures. SCAN achieved the best result with ARI=0.303 (baseline 0.251, +20.6%), and its integration with gene feature fusion was validated as complementary (mean fusion +0.065 ARI). Established hf-mirror.com as the standard solution for cluster HuggingFace data retrieval. Bottlenecks:
⚠️ Pi0.5 OOM remains unresolved (GPU memory insufficient at 150MB), and the baseline assessment is still blocked. ⚠️ The extension of force parameters in visualize_scene.py is complete, but video validation is blocked due to SLURM node permissions issues. ⚠️ Port conflict on Pi0 VLA Server (port 5555 occupied) caused session interruption. Supported by cases involving the brown repeated patches in UNI2. ✅ Implementation of Image-Only Clustering Enhancement Schemes (STEGO/BYOL+GAT/SCAN) (2026-02-19) — Created four model files: STEGOHead/BYOLAdapter/SpatialGATRefiner/SCANHead.
